articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 1. TITLE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Names the ordinance as the Zamboanga City Maritime Coordinating Council ordinance.

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Lists all the government agencies, local leaders, and groups that make up the maritime council, led by the City Mayor.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 3. DUTIES AND FUNCTIONS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Explains what the council does, such as protecting the ocean, stopping crimes and smuggling at sea, and keeping coastal waters safe.

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Makes the City Mayor the leader of the council to manage its day-to-day work.

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires the council to meet at least once every three months to discuss maritime matters.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 7. FUNDING
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets aside at least 500,000 pesos from the city budget to start and run the council.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 8. ANNUAL REPORT
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires the council to report its yearly activities and money spending to the Mayor and City Council.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 9. SEPARABILITY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States that if a court cancels one part of this rule, the rest of the rules will still stay active.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 10. REPEALING CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Cancels older city rules that go against this new maritime council law.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 11. EFFECTIVITY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Makes this law official right after it gets approved.

eli5_summary: Zamboanga City created a special team called the Maritime Coordinating Council to protect the ocean, stop smuggling and crimes at sea, and keep coastal waters safe. The city also gave them a starting budget of 500,000 pesos to help them do their job.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE DECLARING AS PUBLIC NUISANCE ALL ILLEGAL STRUCTURES, OBSTRUCTIONS AND IMPROVEMENTS FOUND WITHIN THE RIVERS OF BOALAN AND TUMAGA, AUTHORIZING ITS SUMMARY ABATEMENT, DEMOLITION AND REMOVAL, AND PROVIDING PENALTIES AND ANNUAL APPROPRIATIONS THEREFOR
authors: HON. JUAN CLIMACO P. ELAGO II

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 1. TITLE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Names the ordinance as the law regarding illegal structures in the Boalan and Tumaga rivers.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 2. DEFINITION OF TERMS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Defines what illegal structures, public nuisances, and the Tumaga River refer to in this ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 3. DECLARATION OF PUBLIC NUISANCE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Declares all illegal structures and improvements in the Boalan and Tumaga rivers as public nuisances.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 4. AUTHORITY TO SUMMARY ABATE, DEMOLISH AND REMOVAL
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Grants city officials the authority to immediately remove and demolish these illegal river structures.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 5. APPROPRIATION
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Allocates funds and equipment to help clear the rivers and prevent flooding.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 6. PENAL CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets fines and possible jail time for anyone who builds illegal structures in the rivers.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 7. ADMINISTRATIVE FINE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Imposes an administrative fine of 5,000 pesos plus removal costs for violators.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 8. SEPARABILITY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Ensures that if one part of this law is found invalid, the rest remains in effect.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 9. REPEALING CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Cancels any previous rules that go against this new ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 10. EFFECTIVITY
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets when this ordinance officially becomes active.

fines.penalty: Fine of not more than Five Thousand Pesos (Php 5,000.00) plus actual cost of removal, or imprisonment of not less than thirty (30) days nor more than six (6) months, or both.

eli5_summary: Building fishponds, houses, or other structures in the Boalan and Tumaga rivers is illegal and blocks water flow, causing floods. This law lets the city quickly tear down these illegal structures and fine or jail the people who built them.
governing_agency: City Environment and Natural Resources Office / City Agriculturist

amendment_details.changes: Modified provisions regarding motorized tricycle routes on Corcuera Street and near City Hall, and specified pedestrian movement enforcement.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE ESTABLISHING AN INCLUSIVE THERAPEUTIC LEARN AND PLAY FACILITY FOR LEARNERS WITH SPECIAL EDUCATIONAL NEEDS AT AYALA CENTRAL SCHOOL SPECIAL EDUCATION (SPED) CENTER ZAMBOANGA CITY AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREOF

articles_and_sections.title: Section 1. Title
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Names the ordinance as the law establishing the special learn and play facility at Ayala Elementary School SPED Center.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 2. Definition of Terms
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Explains special words used in the law like Learners with Special Educational Needs (LSEN), inclusivity, and PWDs.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 3. Declaration of Policies
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States the goal of creating a safe, fun, and therapeutic space for children with different types of disabilities to learn and play.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 4. Site
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Decides that the facility will be built at the Ayala Elementary School SPED Center or another suitable place chosen by the government and DepEd.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 5. Building
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Details that the building will have special toys, books, and equipment designed for children with special needs, planned by the City Engineer's Office.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 6. Appropriation Clause
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets aside 15 million pesos to fund the creation and setup of this facility.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 7. Repealing Clause
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Cancels any older rules that go against this new ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 8. Separability Clause
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Ensures that if one part of this law is found invalid, the rest of the law still stays active.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 9. Effectivity
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States when the law officially starts following government rules.

eli5_summary: Zamboanga City is building a special, fun playground and learning center at the Ayala Elementary School SPED Center for children with special needs. The city is setting aside 15 million pesos to build it with special toys and equipment so these children can play, learn, and grow happily.
governing_agency: City Engineer's Office / Department of Education

official_title: AN ORDINANCE REGULATING SMOKING IN THE CITY OF ZAMBOANGA AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF

articles_and_sections.title: Section 1. TITLE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Gives the official title of this law as the smoking regulation ordinance of Zamboanga City.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 2. PURPOSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Explains that the law aims to protect public health, teach people about smoking risks, regulate tobacco ads, and keep kids from smoking.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 3. COVERAGE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States that this law applies to everyone in enclosed public places, workplaces, public vehicles, and government buildings.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 4. DEFINITION OF TERMS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Defines key terms used in the rule, such as smoking, cigarettes, e-cigarettes, public conveyances, public places, and minors.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 5. SMOKING IN PUBLIC PLACES
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Completely bans smoking in places like schools, elevators, hospitals, gas stations, public transport, and food prep areas.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 6. DESIGNATED SMOKING AREA AND NON-SMOKING AREA
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires public and business places to set up well-ventilated smoking areas with proper warning signs if smoking is allowed.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 7. SALE OF TOBACCO PRODUCTS WITHIN SCHOOL PERIMETERS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Bans selling or giving tobacco products within 100 meters of any school, playground, or youth facility.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 8. PERSONS LIABLE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Lists who can be punished, including public smokers, transport drivers who allow smoking, store workers selling to minors, and business owners allowing illegal smoking.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 9. ENFORCEMENT
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Assigns city offices and local police officers to inspect businesses, post signs, and catch violators.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 10. PENALTIES
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets cash fines, community service, or business permit cancellations for people and establishments breaking the smoking rules.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 11. POSTING OF BILLBOARD
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires the City Engineer's Office to put up public billboards informing citizens about the anti-smoking rules.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 12. SEPARABILITY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Says that if one part of this law is declared invalid, the rest of the law still stays in force.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 13. EFFECTIVITY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States when the ordinance officially takes effect according to local government rules.

fines.penalty: P500.00 fine or 1 day community service
P1,000.00 fine or 2 days community service
P2,000.00 fine or 3 days community service
P5,000.00 fine without prejudice to criminal charges
P5,000.00 fine and revocation or cancellation of Business Permit

eli5_summary: This rule bans smoking cigarettes and e-cigarettes in public places, public transportation, offices, and near schools in Zamboanga City. Businesses must set up specific ventilated smoking areas with warning signs if they want to allow smoking. People or businesses caught breaking the rules will have to pay fines or perform community service.
governing_agency: City Health Office and Smoke-Free Enforcement Team

amended_by_details.changes: Amends certain provisions of the 2013 smoking regulation ordinance to update rules, definitions, penalties, and enforcement mechanisms regarding smoking and vaping in Zamboanga City.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE RENAMING THE EXISTING VETERANS AVENUE FROM ITS JUNCTION WITH CABATO ROAD UP TO THE BRIDGE IN TUMAGA, ZAMBOANGA CITY, AS “JOSE BORJA, SR. ROAD” THEREBY AMENDING ORDINANCE NO. 765, SERIES OF 1967

articles_and_sections.title: Section 1
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section officially changes the name of a specific part of Veterans Avenue to Jose Borja, Sr. Road to honor the late Jose S. Borja, Sr.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 2
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section updates an older law to reflect the new name change.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 3
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section states when the new name officially starts being used.

eli5_summary: This law changes the name of a road in Zamboanga City. A portion of Veterans Avenue is now called Jose Borja, Sr. Road to honor a person who served the city.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE PROHIBITING THE SELLING OF TICKETS OUTSIDE AN OFFICE BOOTH, PLACE OR ANY OFFICE DULY DESIGNATED FOR THE PURPOSE, AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR ANY VIOLATION THEREOF.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 1 - Title
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section names the law the Anti-Scalping Ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 2 - Definition of Scalper
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: A scalper is anyone who sells tickets outside of official ticket booths.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 3 - Definition of Fixer
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: A fixer is someone who helps people get tickets outside of official channels.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 4 - Prohibition
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: It is illegal for scalpers or fixers to sell or help buy tickets outside of official offices.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 5 - Prohibited Acts
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: It is illegal to manage or fund scalping or fixing activities.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 6 - Penalties
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Violators can be fined up to 1,000 pesos or sent to jail for up to six months.

fines.penalty: Fine of not more than 1,000 pesos or imprisonment of not more than 6 months, or both.

eli5_summary: This law stops people from selling tickets for movies, concerts, or travel outside of official ticket booths. If you are caught selling tickets on the street or helping others do so, you could be fined or sent to jail.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE GRANTING MR. FRANCISCO F. ALTEA IV A FRANCHISE TO OPERATE AND MAINTAIN A FLEA MARKET OR “TALIPAPA” AT RIVERSIDE, BARANGAY CURUAN, ZAMBOANGA CITY
authors: Hon. Juan Climaco P. Elago II

articles_and_sections.title: Section 1
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section gives Mr. Francisco F. Altea IV permission to run a small market (talipapa) in Barangay Curuan for five years, provided he follows specific safety, health, and traffic rules.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 2
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section states that if the owner breaks any of the rules, the city can take away or pause his permission to run the market.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 3
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section explains that the rules start following the Local Government Code.

eli5_summary: The city is letting a man named Mr. Altea open a small market in Barangay Curuan. He must keep the area clean, not block the road, and follow all safety and health rules to keep his permit.

amendment_details.changes: Requires the grantee to observe the Barangay Flea Market or Talipapa Ordinance provisions.
Applies distance requirements from public or private markets and public places.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE PROHIBITING ALL SMOKE-BELCHING MOTOR VEHICLES FROM OPERATING, PASSING OR USING ANY STREET OR HIGHWAY WITHIN THE TERRITORIAL JURISDICTION OF ZAMBOANGA CITY AND PROVIDING PENALTY FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF AND THE ESTABLISHMENT, OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF CITY EMISSION TESTING CENTER AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREOF

articles_and_sections.title: Section 1 - Title
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section names the law the Anti-Smoke Belching Ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 2 - Definition of Terms
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section defines technical terms like smoke-belching and emission testing to make the rules clear.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 3 - Enforcement
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section explains how vehicles are checked for smoke and what happens if they fail the test.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 4 - City Emission Testing Center
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section creates a city-run facility to test vehicle smoke levels.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 5 - Authority of the City Emission Testing Center
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section allows the city to work with the Land Transportation Office to issue compliance certificates.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 6 - Certificate of Compliance (COC)
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section explains that vehicles must pass a smoke test to get a certificate valid for six months.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 7 - Certificate of Emission Compliance (CEC)
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section states that vehicles caught and fixed must get a special certificate that does not expire.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 8 - The City Anti-Smoke Belching Task Force
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section creates a team to catch and stop vehicles that are polluting the air.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 9 - Accreditation of NGO and Other Volunteer Environmental Organization
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section allows the city to work with volunteers to help monitor and report smoke-belching vehicles.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 10 - Information and Education Campaign
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section requires the city to teach the public about the importance of clean air and this law.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 11 - Budgetary Provision
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section sets aside money to buy testing equipment and run the testing center.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 12 - Testing Fees and Other Charges
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section lists the costs for getting a vehicle tested.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 13 - Penalties
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section lists the fines for owners whose vehicles fail the smoke test.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 14 - Repealing Clause
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section cancels any old rules that conflict with this new law.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 15 - Effectivity Clause
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section says the law starts working as soon as it is approved.

eli5_summary: This law stops vehicles from blowing thick, black smoke into the air in Zamboanga City. It sets up a testing center to check vehicles and gives fines to owners whose cars are too dirty for the environment.
governing_agency: City Agriculturist Office - Environment and Natural Resources Division

official_title: AN ORDINANCE ESTABLISHING BARANGAY HIGH SCHOOL AT CABALUAY, ZAMBOANGA CITY, AND PROVIDING AN APPROPRIATION THEREFOR

articles_and_sections.title: Section 1 - Title
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section names the ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 2 - Site
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section identifies the land donated by Mr. Basilio Arolinario II as the location for the new school.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 3 - Appropriation
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section sets aside 1.5 million pesos for building and developing the new school.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 4 - Certification of Availability of Funds
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section authorizes the Mayor to ensure the money is ready and included in the city budget.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 5 - Teaching Staff and Other Allied Support
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section declares that the city will work with the Department of Education to provide teachers and support for the school.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 6 - Authority for the Establishment
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section mandates the Mayor to ask the Department of Education for official permission to open the school.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 7 - Effectivity
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section states the school will start operating in the 1992-93 school year.

eli5_summary: The city is building a new high school in Cabaluay to help students who currently have to travel far to get to class. The city is providing money to build the school and will work with the government to make sure there are enough teachers.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE AMENDING SECTION 2 OF ORDINANCE NO. 80, SERIES OF 1988, ENTITLED "AN ORDINANCE CREATING THE CITY HOUSING BOARD AND ESTABLISHING SOME CRITERIA TO QUALIFY BENEFICIARIES UNDER THE CITY HOUSING PROGRAM"

articles_and_sections.title: Section 1
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section updates the list of people who sit on the City Housing Board.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 2
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section states that the new rules start working right away.

eli5_summary: This law changes who is in charge of the City Housing Board. It lists the specific city officials and community representatives who must be part of the group that decides on housing programs.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE CREATING THE COOPERATIVE AND RURAL ECONOMIC ENTERPRISE DEVELOPMENT OFFICE (C.R.E.E.D.O.) AND PROVIDING ANNUAL APPROPRIATIONS THEREFOR

articles_and_sections.title: Section 1 - Title
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section names the law the C.R.E.E.D.O. Ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 2 - Creation
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This creates a new city office called C.R.E.E.D.O. to help local cooperatives and rural businesses with money and support.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 3 - Functions and Powers
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This lists the office's jobs, which include making rules for how they work and reviewing loan applications for businesses.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 4 - Composition
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This explains who runs the office, specifically the City Mayor and a special committee.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 5 - Technical Working Committee
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This creates a group of experts to help check loan applications and make sure the city's money is handled correctly.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 6 - Appropriation
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This sets aside city money to be used for loans to help cooperatives and rural businesses.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 7 - Implementing Guidelines
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This allows the Mayor to create specific rules on how to run this office.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 8 - Separability Clause
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: If one part of this law is found to be invalid, the rest of the law still stays in effect.

eli5_summary: The city is creating a new office called C.R.E.E.D.O. to help local cooperatives and rural businesses grow by providing them with financial assistance and support. This office will be managed by the Mayor and a special committee to ensure the money is used wisely.

amended_by_details.changes: Ordinance No. 373, Series of 2011, is entirely repealed by this ordinance.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE PROVIDING FOR A REVISED CHARTER OF THE CITY OF ZAMBOANGA

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 1
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States that this Ordinance shall be known as the Building Code of Zamboanga City.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 2
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Provides definitions for various words and phrases used throughout the Building Code.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 3
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets the purpose of the Code to promote and safeguard public health, safety, and property through building regulations.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 4
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Defines the scope of the Code, requiring all new buildings, alterations, and repairs to conform with its rules.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 5
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Regulates the use of public property and streets for storing construction materials.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 6
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires protective fencing and temporary sidewalks around building construction sites to protect pedestrians.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 7
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Details how existing buildings must comply with the code during repairs, alterations, or changes in occupancy.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 8
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Allows the use of alternate materials or methods of construction if approved by the City Engineer.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 9
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Empowers the City Engineer to require tests on materials or methods at the owner's expense to ensure compliance.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 10
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Assigns enforcement of the Code to the City Engineer.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 11
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Outlines the specific powers and duties of the City Engineer, including inspections, stop orders, and issuing certificates of occupancy.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 12
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Establishes a Board of Arbitration to resolve disagreements regarding alternate materials and construction methods.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 13
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires a building permit before erecting, constructing, altering, or demolishing any building, with minor exemptions.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 14
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Details the prerequisites and requirements for obtaining a building permit, including application details, plans, specifications, and necessary professional signatures.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 15
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Outlines the process for the issuance of a building permit by the City Engineer after checking compliance with applicable codes and ordinances.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 16
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Explains when a building permit expires if construction is not commenced within a certain timeframe, and the rules for renewal.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 17
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Establishes the schedule of fees required for different types of building permits, construction, repairs, and demolition.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 18
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Mandates that all construction or demolition works under a permit must be supervised by a licensed civil engineer or architect.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 19
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires inspections at various stages of construction, such as foundation, framing, lath, and final inspection.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 20
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Specifies when special supervision and a resident construction inspector are required for large or hazardous projects.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 21
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires the supervising engineer or architect to submit a Certificate of Completion once construction is finished.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 22
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Prohibits the use or occupancy of any new building without securing a Certificate of Occupancy.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 23
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Classifies buildings into different groups (Groups A through I) based on their use or occupancy type.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 24
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Changing the use of a building requires approval and a new Certificate of Occupancy, and the new use must be safer than the old one.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 25
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Buildings with multiple types of occupancy must have proper fire-resistant separations between the different areas.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 26
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Buildings must be erected only in appropriate areas as defined by the Zoning Ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 27
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets building height limits and floor height requirements depending on the street width and zoning.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 28
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Establishes rules for sidewalk construction, widths, repairs, and arcade requirements for specific streets.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 29
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Regulates building projections like eaves, awnings, balconies, and air conditioning units over public spaces.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 30
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Regulates lot occupancy, buildable areas, and firewalls in relation to property lines.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 31
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets specific construction, exit, aisle, and seating regulations for theaters, auditoriums, and assembly halls.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 32
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Regulates building placement and wall openings along property lines for residential, business, and commercial zones.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 33
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires connection to sewerage systems or approved septic tanks with specific dimensions and design requirements.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 34
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Delineates the boundaries of the Fire District for the City of Zamboanga.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 35
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Establishes Fire Zone No. 1 and Fire Zone No. 2 within the Fire District.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 36
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Classifies buildings by types of construction (Type I, II, III) based on their fire resistance.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 37
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Regulates types of buildings permitted within the Fire District, ordering the demolition or relocation of non-compliant Type IV buildings.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 38
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Makes the code applicable to government-owned buildings and lots.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 39
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires specific buildings like hotels, schools, and offices of two or more storeys to have adequate fire escapes.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 40
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Specifies the exact placement and location requirements for fire escapes on buildings.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 41
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Outlines the structural design, materials, and construction guidelines for fire escapes.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 42
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Mandates the installation of approved fire alarm systems in multi-storey hotels, schools, and office buildings.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 43
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires fire hydrants in every storey of multi-storey buildings following specific size and distance standards.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 44
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Establishes general requirements for engineering principles in building design, including material quality, tests, and load testing.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 45
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Details the structural load requirements, including dead loads, live loads for various building types, moving loads, and wind/lateral forces.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 46
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets structural requirements for buildings to withstand earthquake and lateral forces based on building type, height, and formulas.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 47
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Outlines safety rules, shoring, and protections required during excavation and demolition work near other properties.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 48
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Establishes standards for building footings and foundations, including soil bearing capacities and required soil tests.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 49
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Provides detailed specifications for installing and testing pile foundations, including wood, concrete, and steel piles.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 50
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Governs the design, construction, permits, and definitions related to reinforced concrete structures.

articles_and_sections.title: Section (e) to (ag)
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: These sections outline the technical requirements and building standards for using concrete, mixing aggregates, testing materials, placing reinforcement, and setting structural stress limits.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 50 (ah) to (az)
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section outlines the structural engineering requirements and calculations for reinforced concrete buildings, slabs, beams, and columns, including thickness, bending moments, shear, and reinforcement specifications.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 51 - REINFORCED CONCRETE COLUMNS AND WALLS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section outlines the engineering standards, dimensions, and reinforcement requirements for reinforced concrete columns, walls, and footings in construction.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE ESTABLISHING AN INTEGRATED SYSTEM TO PREVENT MENDICANCY IN THE CITY OF ZAMBOANGA, PROVIDING PENALTIES, APPROPRIATING FUNDS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

articles_and_sections.title: Section 1 - Title and Scope
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This law is called the Mendicancy Ordinance and applies to beggars and children under 8 years old found begging on the streets.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 2 - Purpose
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: The goal is to stop begging, protect children from being used for begging, and help beggars get back on their feet.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 3 - Definition of Terms
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Explains that a 'mendicant' is someone who begs for a living, and 'abetting' means helping someone else beg.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 4 - Prohibition
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: It is illegal to beg or to help someone else beg in Zamboanga City.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 5 - Penalty
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Beggars will do community service, while people who help them or exploit children for begging face fines or jail time.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 6 - Exclusionary Clause
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Children under 18 found begging are not treated as criminals but are instead helped by social workers.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 7 - Implementing Clause
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: The city will create a special task force to manage the anti-begging program.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 8 - Appropriations
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: The city is setting aside 500,000 pesos to fund this program.

fines.penalty: 2,000 Pesos or imprisonment not exceeding 1 year, or both.
5,000 Pesos or imprisonment not exceeding 1 year, or both.

eli5_summary: This law makes it illegal to beg on the streets of Zamboanga City. It aims to stop people from using children to beg and provides help and rehabilitation for those who are currently begging.
governing_agency: City Social Welfare and Development Office

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States the city's goal to keep the air clean and free from loud noises caused by modified vehicle exhaust.

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets fines, vehicle impoundment, and muffler destruction for using illegal loud mufflers.

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Allows the city to file criminal cases and court imprisonment for repeat offenders, non-payment, or crimes involving the vehicle.

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets aside 500,000 pesos for equipment needed to enforce this rule.

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Cancels any older rules that go against this new ordinance.

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Says when this law officially starts taking effect.

Four Thousand Pesos (Php4,000.00), confiscation of muffler/exhaust pipe, and the impoundment of the motor vehicle

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Cancels any older rules that conflict with this new ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 9 - Separability Clause
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Ensures that if one part of this law is found invalid, the rest of the law stays in effect.

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States when the ordinance officially becomes active.

fines.penalty: Imprisonment of one (1) year and a fine of One Thousand Pesos (Php1,000.00)
Fine of One Thousand Pesos (Php1,000.00) and confiscation of the contraband
Fine of Three Thousand Pesos (Php3,000.00) and confiscation of the contraband
Fine of Five Thousand Pesos (Php5,000.00) and confiscation of the contraband

eli5_summary: It is now illegal for visitors, staff, or inmates to sneak weapons, drugs, phones, or other prohibited items into Zamboanga City jails. Anyone caught bringing these items inside will face heavy fines, jail time, and have their items taken away. This helps keep everyone inside the jail safe and secure.

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: If one part of this law is found to be invalid, the rest of the law still stays in effect.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 3 - Repealing Clause
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Any old rules that conflict with this new update are now replaced by these new rules.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 4 - Effectivity Clause
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This law starts working according to the rules in the Local Government Code.

eli5_summary: This law makes it easier for more students to get a city scholarship by changing the requirements. Now, the top 25 students from public high schools can apply for help with their college tuition instead of just the top 10.

amendment_details.changes: Expands the scholarship qualification requirement from the top 10 graduates to the top 25 graduates of public high schools, allows 5-year courses, and updates financial assistance distribution rules.

amended_by_details.changes: Further amended provisions previously modified by Ordinance No. 370 regarding academic scholarship grants.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE REGULATING THE ESTABLISHMENT, MAINTENACE AND OPERATION OF NIGHTCLUBS, DAY CLUBS, BARS, COCKTAIL LOUNGES AND BEER GARDENS WITHIN THE TERRITORIAL JURISDICTION OF THE CITY OF ZAMBOANGA, AND REPEALING ORDINANCE No. 987, SERIES OF 1969, FOR THIS PURPOSE

articles_and_sections.title: Section 1 - Scope
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This rule applies to all nightclubs, day clubs, bars, and beer gardens in Zamboanga City.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 2 - Definitions
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section explains what specific terms like 'nightclub', 'bar', and 'hostess' mean for this law.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 3 - Licenses and Permits
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Businesses must get a permit from the Mayor and health office before they can open.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 4 - Suspension or revocation of permit and license
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: If a business breaks the rules, the Mayor can close them down temporarily or take away their permit permanently.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 5 - Prohibitions and/or restrictions as to persons
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Minors, people with weapons, people not dressed properly, or drunk people causing trouble are not allowed inside.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 6 - Restrictions as to persons to be employed
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Workers must be at least 21 years old and have a health certificate to prove they are healthy.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 7 - Regulations and/or restrictions on the operation or management
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Managers must give customers receipts for everything they buy and keep the place safe.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 8 - Duty of the operator
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: The owner is responsible for making sure no illegal activities like gambling or prostitution happen in their business.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 9 - Location
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: These businesses cannot be too close to schools, churches, hospitals, or City Hall.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 10 - Building requirements
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: The building must be safe, well-lit, have proper bathrooms, and be soundproofed so it doesn't bother neighbors.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 11 - Days and hours of operation
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This sets the specific times of day that these businesses are allowed to be open.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 12 - Supervision
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: The Mayor or his representatives will check on these businesses to make sure they follow the rules.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 13 - Mayor's power to promulgate rules and regulations
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: The Mayor can create extra rules as long as they don't go against this law.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 14 - Status of existing nightclubs
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Businesses that were already open must follow noise rules so they don't disturb nearby schools or hospitals.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 15 - Penalties
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: If you break these rules, you could be fined up to 200 pesos or sent to jail for up to six months.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 16 - Separability Clause
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: If one part of this law is found to be invalid, the rest of the law still stays in effect.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 17 - Repealing Clause
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This law replaces the old Ordinance No. 987.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 18 - Effectivity
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This law starts working as soon as it is approved.

fines.penalty: Fine of not more than 200 Pesos or imprisonment of not more than six months, or both.

eli5_summary: This law sets strict rules for nightclubs, bars, and similar businesses in Zamboanga City. It requires them to have proper permits, follow safety and location rules, and ensure their workers are healthy and of age. It also gives the Mayor power to close down businesses that break these rules or allow illegal activities.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE GRANTING EXEMPTION ON THE PAYMENT OF 30% AMUSEMENT TAX FROM THE PROCEEDS OF THE MUSICAL CONCERT “LIVE OUT LOUD”, FEATURING MR. MARTIN NIEVERA WITH SPECIAL GUEST MS. ARA MINA, SPONSORED BY THE ARTURO EUSTAQUIO MEMORIAL SCIENCE HIGH SCHOOL AND UNIVERSIDAD DE ZAMBOANGA ALUMNI ASSOCIATION, INC., ON FEBRUARY 3, 2008 AT 7:30 P.M. AT THE SUMMIT CENTRE, TETUAN, ZAMBOANGA CITY

articles_and_sections.title: Section 1 - Title
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section names the ordinance and explains its purpose, which is to waive the amusement tax for a specific concert.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 2 - Exemption
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section officially grants the concert organizers an exemption from paying the 30% amusement tax.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 3 - Documentation
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: The organizers must provide the City Treasurer with copies of their commercial invoices and contracts.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 4 - Reporting
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Within 10 days after the concert, the organizers must submit a report detailing ticket sales, income, expenses, and any unsold tickets.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 5 - Waiver
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: The city confirms it will not collect the 30% tax for this specific event.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 6 - Publication Costs
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: The organizers are responsible for paying the costs to publish this ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 7 - Effectivity
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: The ordinance becomes active as soon as it is approved.

eli5_summary: The city is allowing a school and alumni association to hold a concert without paying the usual 30% amusement tax. This is because the money raised from the concert will be used to buy school equipment and build a hostel for students.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE RECLASSIFYING A PRODUCTION AGRICULTURAL SUB-ZONE KNOWN AS LOT NO. 778-A-5, CONTAINING AN AREA OF 595 SQUARE METERS, SITUATED AT BARANGAY SAN ROQUE, THIS CITY, TO RESIDENTIAL ZONE-1

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 1
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Reclassifies a specific piece of land (Lot No. 778-A-5 in Barangay San Roque, measuring 595 square meters) from an agricultural zone to a residential zone.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 2
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States that the newly reclassified land must be used in accordance with the city's zoning rules and other applicable laws.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 3
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Ensures that if any part of this ordinance is found illegal, the rest of the ordinance will still remain in effect.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 4
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Cancels any older rules or ordinances that conflict with this new ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 5
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Makes this ordinance effective immediately upon approval.

eli5_summary: A specific piece of land in Barangay San Roque used to be marked for farming, but because it's no longer used for that and surrounded by buildings, the city officially changed its status to residential so people can build homes or use it for residential purposes.
governing_agency: City Zoning Review Committee / Sangguniang Panlungsod

official_title: AN ORDINANCE AMENDING CERTAIN PROVISIONS OF ORDINANCE NO. 185, SERIES OF 1996, ENTITLED “AN ORDINANCE PRESCRIBING THE OPERATION OF TRICYCLES AND GRANTING FRANCHISE FOR THE OPERATION THEREOF WITHIN THE TERRITORIAL JURISDICTION OF THE CITY OF ZAMBOANGA

articles_and_sections.title: Article V - Fares and Freight, Section 1
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets the official tricycle fare at 20 pesos for the first kilometer for one or two passengers, plus 5 pesos for a third passenger and 5 pesos for each extra kilometer. It also mandates discounts for seniors, PWDs, and students, and requires an official fare chart to be posted inside the tricycle.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 2
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States that this ordinance takes effect immediately once approved.

eli5_summary: This ordinance updates the official tricycle passenger fares in Zamboanga City, setting the standard rate to 20 pesos for the first kilometer for up to two passengers. It mandates fare discounts for senior citizens, students, and persons with disabilities, and requires all tricycles to visibly post an official fare matrix.

amendment_details.changes: Updates the provisions regarding fares and freight under Article V, establishing specific fare rates and requirements for fare matrices.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE REGULATING AND PENALIZING THE CONSTRUCTION, INSTALLATION, POSTING OR DISPLAY OF TEMPORARY ARCHES AND BILLBOARDS, BANNERS, STREAMERS, PLACARDS, COMMERCIAL AND NON-COMMERCIAL ADVERTISEMENT OR THE FLYING OF SIGNS, WITHIN THE CITY OF ZAMBOANGA

articles_and_sections.title: Section 1 - Regulation
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: You need permission from the City Mayor to put up signs, banners, or arches on public property.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 2 - Removal
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: You must take down your signs or banners within seven days after your permit expires or if they become messy.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 3 - Fees
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: You have to pay a fee and a deposit to put up signs, unless it is for political, religious, or school events.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 4 - Penalties
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: If you break these rules, you may have to pay a fine or go to jail.

fines.penalty: Fine of P3,000.00 to P5,000.00 or imprisonment of 10 to 30 days, or both.
Fine of P300.00

eli5_summary: This rule says you need permission from the Mayor to put up signs, banners, or arches in public places. If you don't take them down when you are supposed to, or if you don't follow the rules, you might have to pay a fine or go to jail.

amendment_details.changes: The entire ordinance is repealed by Section 5.

official_title: COMPREHENSIVE ANTI-DISCRIMINATION ORDINANCE IN THE CITY OF ZAMBOANGA
authors: HON. JUAN CLIMACO P. ELAGO II

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 1. TITLE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States the official name of the ordinance, which is the Comprehensive Anti-Discrimination Ordinance of the City of Zamboanga.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 2. DECLARATION OF POLICY
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Declares that everyone has the right to be free from discrimination regardless of background, identity, or beliefs.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 3. COVERAGE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Lists the various traits and statuses protected under this anti-discrimination rule.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 4. DEFINITION OF TERMS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Explains specific terms used in the ordinance such as age, disability, gender identity, and public ridicule so everyone understands what they mean.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 5. PROHIBITED ACTS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Details the specific unfair actions that are banned, such as denying services, kicking students out of school, or mocking people based on protected traits.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 6. PERSONS LIABLE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Explains who can be held legally responsible if discrimination happens, including company and organization heads.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 7. THE CREATION OF AN ANTI-DISCRIMINATION DESK
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires all barangays, government offices, and private workplaces to set up a special desk to handle discrimination complaints.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 8. INFORMATION CAMPAIGN AND ANTI-DISCRIMINATION PROGRAMS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Directs the city to spread awareness about this law to the public shortly after approval.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 9. PENALTY
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets the punishment for breaking the law, which can include a 5,000 peso fine, up to a year in prison, or both, plus a mandatory seminar.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 10. APPROPRIATION CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets aside 250,000 pesos to fund campaign materials and public awareness.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 11. SEPARABILITY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Ensures that if one part of this law is found illegal by a court, the rest of the law still stays active.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 12. REPEALING CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Cancels older rules or ordinances that conflict with this new anti-discrimination law.

fines.penalty: Fine of FIVE THOUSAND PESOS (Php5,000.00), or imprisonment of not more than ONE YEAR, or BOTH, plus a mandatory anti-discrimination seminar.

eli5_summary: Zamboanga City passed a law to protect everyone from being treated unfairly or bullied because of their race, religion, gender, age, disability, or health status. If anyone discriminates against another person, they can face fines, jail time, or both. Every barangay and workplace must also set up a desk to help report and stop discrimination.
governing_agency: Sangguniang Panlungsod / City Information Office / Barangay Anti-Discrimination Desks

official_title: AN ORDINANCE BANNING THE USE, SALE, POSSESSION, DISTRIBUTION, STORAGE, AND MANUFACTURE OF FIRECRACKERS AND PYROTECHNIC DEVICES WITHIN THE TERRITORIAL JURISDICTION OF ZAMBOANGA CITY
authors: Hon. Juan Climaco P. Elago II

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 1. TITLE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Names the ordinance as 'The Firecracker Ban Ordinance of 2014'.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 2. BAN ON FIRECRACKERS AND PYROTECHNIC DEVICES
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Prohibits using, selling, keeping, or making firecrackers and fireworks anywhere in Zamboanga City, except when passing through as cargo.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 3. TRANSSHIPMENT OF FIRECRACKERS AND PYROTECHNIC DEVICES
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Allows firecrackers to pass through the city as cargo under strict security and temporary storage rules.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 4. INFORMATION DISSEMINATION
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires city offices to educate the public about the firecracker ban and its safety reasons.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 5. PENAL PROVISION
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets jail time and court fines for anyone caught violating the firecracker ban.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 6. ADMINISTRATIVE FINES
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets escalating cash fines and possible business closure for violators caught by administrative authorities.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 7. IMPLEMENTING AGENCIES
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Directs police, local leaders, and security agencies to enforce the firecracker ban.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 8. IMPLEMENTING RULES AND REGULATIONS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Creates a committee led by the Mayor to make sure the ordinance is properly carried out.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 9. SEPARABILITY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Ensures the rest of the law remains valid even if a part of it is found illegal.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 10. REPEALING CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Cancels any older city rules that conflict with this ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 11. EFFECTIVITY
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States that the law takes effect immediately after approval.

fines.penalty: One Thousand Pesos (P1,000.00) administrative fine; penal fine of not less than P1,000 nor more than P5,000 or imprisonment of not less than 6 months nor more than 1 year, or both at the court's discretion.
Three Thousand Pesos (P3,000.00) administrative fine.
Five Thousand Pesos (P5,000.00) administrative fine, confiscation of items, and business closure order.

eli5_summary: It is completely illegal to use, sell, keep, or make firecrackers and fireworks in Zamboanga City. This rule is in place to keep everyone safe and prevent injuries and fires. Anyone caught breaking this rule will face fines, confiscation of their items, or even jail time.
governing_agency: Philippine National Police (PNP) and City Government

amended_by_details.changes: Amended or modified to align with the regulations on commercial fireworks.
Lifts the ban on the use, sale, possession, distribution, and storage of consumer pyrotechnics specifically from December 1 to January 6, while keeping the firecracker ban active.

Modified to allow professional display pyrotechnics and commercial fireworks during specific special public occasions or celebrations, while keeping the general ban on regular consumer firecrackers and pyrotechnics intact.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE GRANTING AMNESTY IN THE PAYMENT OF PENALTY SURCHAGE ON REAL PROPERTIES WITHIN THE TERRITORIAL JURISDICTION OF THE CITY OF ZAMBOANGA

articles_and_sections.title: Section 1 - Coverage
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section says that people who haven't paid their property taxes on time can get a break on the extra fees and penalties for taxes owed up to September 30, 1994.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 2 - Duration
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section sets a deadline, saying you must take advantage of this tax break by March 31, 1995.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 3 - Effectivity
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section states that the new rule starts working as soon as it is officially approved.

eli5_summary: If you were late paying your property taxes before September 1994, the city is letting you pay just the tax amount without the extra penalty fees. You had until March 1995 to pay these taxes to get this special discount.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE GRANTING MEDICAL CARE AND HOSPITALIZATION ASSISTANCE TO MEMBERS OF THE PHILIPPINE NATIONAL POLICE, MEMBERS OF THE CITIZENS ARMED FORCES GEOGRAPHICAL UNITS (CAFGU), OFFICIALS AND EMPLOYEES OF THE CITY GOVERNMENT AND ALL BARANGAY OFFICIALS IN THE CITY OF ZAMBOANGA AND PROVIDING AN APPROPRIATION THEREFOR

articles_and_sections.title: Section 1 - Title
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section names the ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 2 - Coverage
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section lists the specific public servants, such as police, CAFGU members, city employees, and barangay officials, who are eligible for help.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 3 - Requirement for Coverage
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: To get help, the person must have been injured while doing their official job duties.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 4 - Hospital Preference
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Patients must go to a government hospital unless there is a special security or medical reason to go elsewhere.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 5 - Appropriation
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: The city sets aside 300,000 pesos every year to pay for these medical costs.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 6 - Disbursement/Releases
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: The city pays the hospital or doctor directly for the medical bills.

eli5_summary: This law provides financial help for medical and hospital bills to police, CAFGU members, city workers, and barangay officials who get hurt while working. The city sets aside money every year to pay these bills directly to the hospitals or doctors.

amended_by_details.changes: Section 1 was amended to change the date of the Zamboanga City town fiesta (Fiesta Pilar) from December 8th to October 12th.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE RECLASSIFYING A PRODUCTION AGRICULTURAL SUB-ZONE KNOWN AS LOT NO. 1980-A, CONTAINING AN AREA OF 38,625 SQUARE METERS, SITUATED AT BARANGAY SALAAN, THIS CITY, TO RESIDENTIAL ZONE-1

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 1
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Reclassifies a specific parcel of land (Lot No. 1980-A) in Barangay Salaan from agricultural to a residential zone.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 2
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States that the newly reclassified land must be used in accordance with the city zoning rules and laws.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 3
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Ensures that if any part of this law is found invalid, the rest of the law still remains active.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 4
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Cancels any older local rules that conflict with this ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 5
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Makes the ordinance effective immediately upon approval.

eli5_summary: A piece of farmland in Barangay Salaan is officially changed into a residential area so people can build homes or other non-agricultural buildings there.

amendment_details.changes: Replaces Section 2 to update the official composition and members of the City Housing Board.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE REQUIRING THE MANDATORY NUMBERING OF EVERY RESIDENTIAL HOUSE, COMMERCIAL AND INDUSTRIAL BUILDING, PRESCRIBING RULES AND REGULATIONS FOR ITS IMPLEMENTATION AND IMPOSING PENALTY FOR VIOLATION AND PROVIDING AN APPROPRIATION THEREFOR

articles_and_sections.title: Section 1 - Title
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section names the ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 2 - Mandatory Numbering
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: All buildings in the city must have a number.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 3 - Nature of Number
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: The house number must be made of tin with a white background and red numbers.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 4 - Payment
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Owners must pay 50 pesos to get their house number.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 5 & 6 - Penalized Acts
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: It is against the law to damage, remove, or refuse to have a house number.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 7, 8 & 9 - Implementation and Records
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: The City Engineer and Barangay Captains will manage the numbering and keep records of all houses.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 10 - Penalty
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: If you break these rules, you could be fined between 200 and 1,000 pesos or go to jail for up to a year.

fines.penalty: Fine of 200 to 1,000 pesos or imprisonment of 30 days to 1 year, or both.

eli5_summary: Every house and building in Zamboanga City must have a specific number made of tin to help mail carriers find addresses. You have to pay 50 pesos for this number, and you are not allowed to remove or damage it.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE CREATING THE BARANGAY OF CAMINO NUEVO OUT OF THE EXISTING BARANGAY OF CANELAR IN ZAMBOANGA CITY AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS FOR THE INCIDENTAL EXPENSES THEREFOR

articles_and_sections.title: Section 1 - Title
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section names the ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 2 - Creation
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section officially creates the new Barangay of Camino Nuevo from part of the existing Barangay Canelar.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 3 - Political Boundaries
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section defines the specific streets and landmarks that mark the borders of the new barangay.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 4 - General Powers and Attributes
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section gives the new barangay the same legal rights and powers as all other barangays.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 5 - Officials and Offices
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section describes the leadership team for the new barangay, including elected and appointed positions.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 6 - Powers and Duties
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section explains what the barangay leaders are responsible for doing.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 7 - Appropriations
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section sets aside 6,000 pesos to help pay for the costs of starting the new barangay.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 10 - Effectivity
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section states that the new barangay only becomes official if the people living there vote 'yes' in a special election.

eli5_summary: This law splits the large Barangay Canelar into two smaller barangays, creating a new one called Barangay Camino Nuevo. This was done to make it easier for the government to provide services to the people living there. The change only happens if the residents vote for it in a special election.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE RECLASSIFYING A PRODUCTION AGRICULTURAL SUB-ZONE KNOWN AS LOT NO. 93-C-6, CONTAINING AN AREA OF 600 SQUARE SINK, SITUATED AT BARANGAY LUNZURAN, THIS CITY, TO RESIDENTIAL ZONE-1

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 1
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Reclassifies a specific 600-square meter plot of land in Barangay Lunzuran from agricultural to residential use.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 2
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires the land to be used strictly following the city's zoning rules and laws.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 3
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Ensures that if any part of this rule is found illegal, the rest of it still works.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 4
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Cancels any older local rules that conflict with this ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 5
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States that this ordinance becomes active right after it is approved.

eli5_summary: The city is officially changing a small piece of farm land in Barangay Lunzuran so that houses can be built on it instead. Because the land can no longer be used for growing crops like rice, the city approved turning it into a residential area.

official_title: AN ENABLING ORDINANCE IMPLEMENTING AND ENFORCING THE PROVISIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9208, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS “THE ANTI-TRAFFICKING IN PERSONS ACT OF 2003,” IN THE CITY OF ZAMBOANGA AND PRESCRIBING PENALTIES FOR CERTAIN ACTS OR OMISSIONS VIOLATIVE OF THIS ORDINANCE, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

articles_and_sections.title: Section 1 - Title
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section names the ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 2 - Definition of Terms
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section explains what specific words like trafficking, child, and sex tourism mean in this law.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 3 - Role of the City Government
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: The city promises to help protect victims of human trafficking and catch the people who do it.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 4 - Implementing Agency
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This creates a special committee (CIACAT) to lead the fight against human trafficking in the city.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 5 - Functions of the City Inter-Agency Committee
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This lists the specific jobs the committee must do, like making plans and helping victims.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 6 - Monitoring and Documentation of Cases
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: The city social worker will keep track of all trafficking cases.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 7 - The Local Inter-Agency Task Force
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This creates task forces to watch over sea, land, and air travel for trafficking.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 8 - Visitorial Powers
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: The Mayor has the power to inspect buildings or houses suspected of being used for trafficking.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 9 - Deputization of Barangays
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Barangay officials are given the power to help enforce this law and check for legal recruitment papers.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 10 - Information and Education Campaign
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: The city will teach people about the dangers of human trafficking through posters and ads.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 11 - Support of Community-Based Initiatives
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: The city will support groups that help victims of trafficking.

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Establishes criminal penalties, including fines and imprisonment, for tourism businesses that break the rules.

articles_and_sections.title: Article VIII - Final Provisions
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Covers the transfer of existing personnel, sunset reviews, and when the law officially takes effect.

fines.penalty: A fine of Two Thousand Pesos (P2,000.00) per day of violation.
A fine of Three Thousand Pesos (P3,000.00) per day of violation.
A fine of Five Thousand Pesos (P5,000.00) and possible closure of the establishment and/or revocation of the business permit.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE PROHIBITING ANY PERSON, PARTNERSHIP OR CORPORATION FROM HUNTING, FISHING, BATHING, WASHING, CAMPING, GATHERING FOREST PRODUCTS, CUTTING SHRUBS, FIREWOOD, TIMBER OR LOG, OCCUPYING, SQUATTING, CULTIVATING OR CLEARING, OR IN ANY MANNER ENTER, TRESSPASS OR ENCROACH UPON ANY PART WITHIN THE DEFINED BOUNDARIES OF THE FOREST RESERVATION THAT FORM PART OF THE ZAMBOANGA CITY WATERSHED AREA, AND OVER ALL TERRITORY WITHIN THE DRAINAGE AREA OF THE WATER SOURCE OF THE ZAMBOANGA CITY WATER DISTRICT.

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Anyone found inside the watershed area without permission is automatically considered a trespasser.

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: If you are caught in the watershed with tools for cutting trees, the law assumes you are logging illegally and your tools will be taken away.

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Companies, their leaders, and anyone who pays for illegal logging activities are held responsible for breaking this law.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 5
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Zamboanga City Water District guards and environmental officials are the ones in charge of enforcing these rules.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 6
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Violators can be fined up to 1,000 pesos or sent to jail for up to six months, or both.

fines.penalty: Fine of not more than P1,000.00 or imprisonment of not more than six (6) months, or both.

eli5_summary: This law protects the city's water supply by making it illegal to enter, camp, hunt, or cut trees in the Zamboanga City watershed area. If you break these rules, you could face a fine or go to jail.

official_title: FORMULATION AND ADOPTION OF COMPREHENSIVE COASTAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT PLAN FOR THE CITY OF ZAMBOANGA TO ENSURE SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT OF THE CITY COASTAL AND MARINE ENVIRONMENT AND RESOURCES AND ESTABLISHING THE SUPPORTING MECHANISM THEREOF FOR ITS IMPLEMENTATION, AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR

articles_and_sections.title: Section 1 - Title

articles_and_sections.title: Section 2 - The Coastal Resources Management Plan

articles_and_sections.title: Section 3 - Lead Agency

articles_and_sections.title: Section 4 - Scope and Coverage

articles_and_sections.title: Section 5 - Participatory Coastal Resource Assessment
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Local community members and officials will help gather information to better manage coastal resources.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 6 - Concerns in the development of CCRM
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section lists the goals for the plan, such as protecting marine life, promoting tourism, and managing waste.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 7 - Barangay Participation
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Local barangays are required to help identify coastal issues and implement solutions.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 8 - Budget Appropriation for CCRM Plan

articles_and_sections.title: Section 9 - Effectivity

eli5_summary: This law creates a plan to take better care of Zamboanga City's beaches, oceans, and marine life. It gives the city government a budget to protect these areas and asks local communities to help keep our waters clean and healthy.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE PRESCRIBING GUIDELINES TO REGULATE THE MODE OF OPERATION OF VIDEO COMPUTER PARLORS AND PROVIDING PENALTY FOR VIOLATIONS THEREFORE

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This law applies to all video computer parlors operating within Zamboanga City.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 4 - Requirements

articles_and_sections.title: Section 5 - Board of Reviewers
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: A group will be created to check if these shops are following the rules.

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Shop owners must pay specific permit and amusement taxes to the city.

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: If you break these rules, you may be fined or sent to jail.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 10 - Separability Clause
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: If one part of this law is found to be illegal, the rest of the law still stays in effect.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 11 - Repealing Clause
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Any old rules that conflict with this new law are now cancelled.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 12 - Effectivity
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This law starts working as soon as it is approved.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE FURTHER AMENDING CERTAIN SECTIONS OF ORDINANCE NO. 259, SERIES OF 2004, ENTITLED, “AN ORDINANCE ENACTING THE ZAMBOANGA CITY INVESTMENT INCENTIVE CODE OF 2004, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES”.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 1 - Amending Section 3 (Definition of Terms)

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Lists 15 preferred business sectors (like agriculture, BPO, green projects, and tourism) that qualify for special city incentives every three years.

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets rules on minimum investment amounts and required number of employees for new businesses to qualify for city incentives.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE ESTABLISHING THE BIORISK DESK OFFICER, AND THE BIORISK PROTOCOLS, PENALTIES AND FUNDING
authors: HON. JUAN CLIMACO P. ELAGO II

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 1. TITLE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Names the ordinance as the Biorisk Management Ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 2. SCOPE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Covers all local schools, factories, hospitals, farms, and businesses that handle dangerous chemicals, biological agents, or radioactive materials.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 3. OBJECTIVES
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets safety rules for hazardous materials and creates a special Biorisk desk and technical committee to oversee them.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 4. DEFINITIONS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Defines key terms like biosafety, biosecurity, bio-hazards, and biorisk management so everyone understands the technical words used.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 5. ESTABLISHMENT
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Creates a Biosafety Desk Office under the disaster management office to regulate hazards and educate the public.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 6. BUSINESS PERMIT
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires all businesses applying for a permit to include biorisk protocols in their application.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 7. RISK PROTOCOL
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Empowers the Mayor to issue official rules for managing bio-radioactive chemical risks.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 8. APPLICATION OF PROTOCOL
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Reiterates that businesses must follow specific biochemical hazard protocols to get their permits.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 9. QUARANTINE PROTOCOLS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Allows local and national governments to implement quarantine measures when necessary.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 10. FUNDING
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Ensures money is set aside in the city budget to carry out this law.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 11. PENALTIES
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Lists fines and business suspensions for establishments that break safety rules, scaling up to permanent closure for repeat offenses.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 12. REPEALING CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Cancels any older city rules that conflict with this ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 13. SEPARABILITY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States that if one part of this law is found illegal, the rest of the law still remains valid.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 14. EFFECTIVITY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Makes the ordinance official 15 days after it is published in a local newspaper.

fines.penalty: Php 5,000.00 per violation
Php 5,000.00 per violation and suspension of Business for 30 days
Php 5,000.00 per violation and suspension of Business for 90 days
Php 5,000.00 per violation, suspension of business for 120 days with violation rectified, complied, and completed
Termination of Business and Closure

eli5_summary: This ordinance creates a special safety office in Zamboanga City to handle dangerous biological, chemical, and radioactive materials. Local businesses that handle these materials must follow strict safety rules and include them in their business permits, or face fines and possible closure.

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Cancels any older rules that go against this new ordinance.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE AMENDING CERTAIN PROVISIONS OF ORDINANCE NO. 268, SERIES OF 2005, ENTITLED “AN ORDINANCE PRESCRIBING THE GUIDELINES, RULES AND REGULATIONS FOR THE RESETTLEMENT AND SOCIALIZED HOUSING PROJECTS OF THE CITY OF ZAMBOANGA AND THE CREATION OF THE CITY HOUSING AND LAND MANAGEMENT OFFICE” AND PROVIDING CONDONATION OF INTERESTS, PENALTIES AND SURCHARGES FOR BENEFICIARIES OF EXISTING RESETTLEMENT SITES

articles_and_sections.title: Section 8

Extends the condonation period under Section 4 until July 20, 2023.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE REGULATING THE FUND RAISING ACTIVITIES WITHIN THE TERRITORIAL JURISDICTION OF ZAMBOANGA CITY AND PROVIDING PENALTY THEREFOR

articles_and_sections.title: Section 1 - Policy

articles_and_sections.title: Section 4 - Penalties

eli5_summary: This law stops city officials and police from using their power to ask for money for private fundraising projects. It makes sure that government leaders don't pressure people into giving money for things the city isn't actually supporting.
