official_title: AN ORDINANCE PROVIDING FOR A COMMUNITY-BASED PSYCHIATRIC, NEUROLOGICAL AND PSYCHOSOCIAL HEALTH SERVICES AND PROPER REFERRAL SYSTEM IN THE CITY OF ZAMBOANGA AND APPROPRIATING THE NECESSARY FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
co_authors: HON. JUAN CLIMACO P. ELAGO II

articles_and_sections.title: Article I - Title, Policy, Objective, and Definition of Terms
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets the name of the law as the Mental Health Ordinance and defines important terms like mental health, illness, and professionals.

articles_and_sections.title: Article II - Zamboanga City Mental Health Council
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Creates a special council led by the Mayor to plan and oversee mental health programs in the city.

articles_and_sections.title: Article III - Psychosocial Care Delivery and Referral System in the Community Level
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Explains how people can get mental health checkups and counseling at local barangay health centers and how severe cases are referred to doctors.

articles_and_sections.title: Article IV - Drug Addiction and Suicide Prevention Services
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Establishes drug screening, rehab efforts, and 24/7 suicide prevention hotlines.

articles_and_sections.title: Article V - Rights of Service Users and Consent to Treatment
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Protects the human rights, privacy, and right to choose treatment for patients receiving mental health care.

articles_and_sections.title: Article VI - Mental Healthcare Trainings
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires local health workers and barangay officials to take training on how to handle mental health issues.

articles_and_sections.title: Article VII - Institutionalizing a Telepsychiatry/Telepsychology Service in the Barangays
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets up online video checkups and a 24/7 helpline so residents can talk to mental health professionals from their local barangay.

articles_and_sections.title: Article VIII - Promotion of Mental Health and Public Awareness
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Promotes mental health awareness in schools, workplaces, and the media while preventing harmful reporting on suicide.

articles_and_sections.title: Article IX - Patient's Right to Treatment and Confidentiality
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Guarantees that patients get proper medical standards of care, privacy of records, and voluntary admission rules.

articles_and_sections.title: Article X - Final Provisions
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets aside an initial budget of at least 7 million pesos to start funding this mental health program.

eli5_summary: Zamboanga City created a new program to provide free or accessible mental health checkups, counseling, and 24/7 hotlines right in your local barangays. It protects patients' privacy and rights while training local health workers to help people dealing with stress, depression, or other mental health needs.
governing_agency: City Health Office / Zamboanga City Mental Health Council

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 7. EFFECTIVITY CLAUSE

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section grants Mr. Noel Arquiza permission to run a small market in Barangay Mercedes for five years, provided he follows specific rules about safety, cleanliness, and location.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 2
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section states that if the owner breaks any of the rules, the city has the power to take away or pause his permission to run the market.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 3
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section requires the owner to apply for a renewal of his permit two months before his current permission expires.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 4
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section explains that the rules of this permit start following the standard local government laws.

eli5_summary: The city is giving Mr. Noel Arquiza permission to open a small market in Barangay Mercedes for five years. He must keep the area clean, follow safety rules, and make sure he doesn't block the road or sidewalk.

amendment_details.changes: Amended Article VI, Sections 3 and 4 to clarify the procedure for granting zoning exceptions and variances, and Article VIII, Section 3 to specify the powers and duties of the Zoning Officer. The original zoning ordinance remains functional.

amended_by_details.changes: Replaced entirely by the new franchise grant under Ordinance No. 497.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE AUTHORIZING THE SELLING OF SOUVENIR ITEMS AND OTHER COMMEMORATIVE ITEMS, CHABACANO BOOKS AND OTHER PUBLICATIONS, AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTS, SEEDLINGS, AND OTHER ITEMS AND PRODUCTS PRODUCED, DEVELOPED, CREATED AND/OR OWNED BY THE CITY GOVERNMENT OF ZAMBOANGA AND IMPOSING REASONABLE FEES ON CERTAIN SERVICES

articles_and_sections.title: Section 1 - Authorization to Sell
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section allows the city to sell souvenirs, books, agricultural products, and seedlings to the public at reasonable prices.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 2 - El Comite de Recuerdos y Cosechas de Zamboanga
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This creates a special committee led by the Mayor to manage the sale of these items and services.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 3 - Duties and Functions
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: The committee is responsible for deciding what to sell, setting prices, and promoting the city's products.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 4 - Appropriation
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: The city sets aside one million pesos to fund this project.

eli5_summary: The city government is now allowed to sell its own souvenirs, books, and farm products to the public. A special committee will manage these sales and set fair prices to help promote Zamboanga's culture and products.
governing_agency: El Comite de Recuerdos y Cosechas de Zamboanga

amendment_details.changes: Expands on the harvesting, gathering, and selling of agricultural products produced by the city.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE AMENDING SECTIONS 2, 3 & 4 OF ORDINANCE NO. 231, SERIES OF 2000, ENTITLED “AN ORDINANCE PROVIDING FINANCIAL INCENTIVES TO ATHLETICS/PLAYERS AND COACHES/TRAINORS WHO CAN ACHIEVE HIGH HONORS IN THE OLYMPICS GAMES, SEA GAMES AND ASIAN GAMES.”
authors: Hon. Juan Climaco P. Elago II

articles_and_sections.title: Section 2 - Definition of Terms
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section defines who qualifies as a coach, athlete, or medalist and what specific sports competitions are covered by the ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 3 - Coverage
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section explains that only athletes who live in Zamboanga City can receive these cash rewards and sets the deadline for filing claims.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 4 - Amount of Incentives
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section lists the specific cash prizes for winning gold, silver, or bronze medals in different international sports events.

eli5_summary: This law gives cash rewards to athletes from Zamboanga City who win medals in big international sports competitions like the Olympics. It also provides a share of these rewards to their coaches and trainers.

amendment_details.changes: Amended Sections 2, 3, and 4 to update definitions, coverage, filing deadlines, and the specific monetary amounts for athletic financial incentives.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE STRENGTHENING THE CITY’S INTERFAITH PROGRAM THROUGH THE CREATION OF THE CITY INTERFAITH COUNCIL AND MANDATING THE ESTABLISHMENT OF INTERFAITH DESKS AND FOCAL PERSONS AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER RELATED PURPOSES
authors: HON. JUAN CLIMACO P. ELAGO II

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 1. CREATION OF THE INTERFAITH COUNCIL
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Creates the Zamboanga City Interfaith Council to recommend policies, ensure consistency in interfaith dialogues, and build partnerships with religious and civil groups.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 2. COMPOSITION
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Lists the members of the Council, which includes the City Mayor as Chair, religious leaders from various faiths, indigenous representatives, and community organizations.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 3. SUPPORT STRUCTURE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Allows other government offices and non-government organizations to help the Council when needed.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 4. CREATION OF INTERFAITH DESKS AND FOCAL PERSONS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires all city and national government offices, as well as barangays, to set up an interfaith desk and assign a trained person to handle interfaith programs.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 5. FUNDING
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets aside an initial fund of Two Million Pesos (Php 2,000,000.00) from the City Government to support the Council's activities.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 6. SEPARABILITY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States that if any part of this law is declared invalid, the rest of the law will still remain in effect.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 7. REPEALING CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Cancels any older city rules or parts of rules that go against this new ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 8. EFFECTIVITY
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States that the ordinance becomes official 15 days after being published in a newspaper following its approval.

eli5_summary: Zamboanga City created a special Interfaith Council and set up interfaith desks in local government offices to promote peace, understanding, and cooperation among people of different religions. The city also provided an initial budget of Two Million Pesos to fund these peace-building programs and activities.

amendment_details.changes: Modified provisions regarding motorized tricycle routes on Corcuera Street and near City Hall, and specified pedestrian movement enforcement.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE RECLASSIFYING A PRODUCTION AGRICULTURAL SUB-ZONE KNOWN AS LOT NO. 74, CONTAINING AN AREA OF 85,673 SQUARE METERS, SITUATED AT BARANGAY BOALAN, THIS CITY, TO RESIDENTIAL ZONE-1

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 1

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 2

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 3

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 4

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 5

official_title: AN ORDINANCE AMENDING PARAGRAPH 3, SECTION 2, ARTICLE III AND SECTION 2, ARTICLE IV OF ORDINANCE NO. 15, SERIES OF 1977, ENTITLED “TRAFFIC CODE OF 1977 FOR ZAMBOANGA CITY.”

articles_and_sections.title: Article III - Parking Regulations
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section sets specific rules for parking on Normal Road, allowing only southside parallel parking between Zamboanga-Labuan Road and Justice Roseller T. Lim Boulevard.

articles_and_sections.title: Article IV - Routing of Traffic
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section declares Normal Road as a one-way street for traffic moving east to west between Zamboanga-Labuan Road and Justice Roseller T. Lim Boulevard.

eli5_summary: This law changes how cars park and drive on Normal Road in Zamboanga City. It makes the road one-way for traffic and limits parking to only one side of the street to help traffic flow better.

amendment_details.changes: Amends Paragraph 3, Section 2, Article III and Section 2, Article IV regarding parking and one-way traffic on Normal Road.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE GRANTING AMNESTY IN THE PAYMENT OF PENALTY/SURCHARGE ON REAL PROPERTIES WITHIN THE TERRITORIAL JURISDICTION OF THE CITY OF ZAMBOANGA

articles_and_sections.title: Section 1
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section allows people who haven't paid their property taxes from before 2002 to avoid paying extra penalty fees.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 2
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section sets a deadline of June 30, 2002, for people to take advantage of this tax penalty forgiveness.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 3
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section states that the rule starts working as soon as it is officially approved.

eli5_summary: If you owed property taxes before 2002, the city decided to forgive the extra penalty fees you would normally have to pay. You had until June 30, 2002, to pay your base taxes without those extra charges.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE REPEALING ORDINANCE NO. 772 ENTITLED “AN ORDINANCE RECLASSIFYING A PRODUCTION AGRICULTURAL SUBZONE KNOWN AS LOT NO. 121, CONTAINING AN AREA OF 15,943 SQUARE METERS, SITUATED AT BARANGAY BOALAN, THIS CITY, TO RESIDENTIAL ZONE-1,” AND REVERTING LOT NO. 121’S CLASSIFICATION TO PRODUCTION AGRICULTURAL SUB-ZONE PURSUANT TO ORDINANCE NO. 516

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 1. REPEAL
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Cancels an old rule that changed a piece of land in Barangay Boalan into residential property, and changes it back to agricultural land.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 2. SEPARABILITY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States that if one part of this rule is found illegal, the rest of the rule still applies.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 3. REPEALING CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Removes any older rules that conflict with this new one.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 4. EFFECTIVITY
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Says when this new rule officially starts working.

eli5_summary: This ordinance changes a specific piece of land in Barangay Boalan back to farming land because the property owner was never asked or told about the previous change to residential land.

amendment_details.changes: Completely repeals Ordinance No. 772 which previously reclassified Lot No. 121 from agricultural to residential, thereby reverting it back to a production agricultural sub-zone under Ordinance No. 516.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE ESTABLISHING A HIGH SCHOOL IN THE BARANGAY OF CALARIAN, ZAMBOANGA CITY, AND PROVIDING AN INITIAL APPROPRIATION THEREOF

articles_and_sections.title: Section 1 - Title
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section names the ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 2 - Site
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section identifies that the school will be located in Barangay Calarian.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 3 - Initial Appropriation
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section sets aside 2.1 million pesos to build the school.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 4 - Source of Initial Appropriation
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section explains that the money for the school comes from city infrastructure funds.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 5 - Maintenance and Other Operating Expenses
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section provides an extra 50,000 pesos annually for school maintenance.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 6 - Teaching Staff, Administrative Personnel and Other Allied Support
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section states that the Department of Education will manage the teachers and staff.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 7 - Procedure for Processing
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section outlines the steps the Mayor and school officials must take to get the school approved by the government.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 8 - Commencement of Classes
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section explains when classes will start once the school is officially authorized.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 9 - Temporary Holding of Classes
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section allows students to use the local elementary school building until the new high school is finished.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 10
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section states the ordinance takes effect immediately upon approval.

eli5_summary: This ordinance creates a new public high school in Barangay Calarian to help local students get an education closer to home. It provides the money to build the school and explains how teachers will be hired and where classes will be held while the building is being constructed.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE RECLASSIFYING A PRODUCTION AGRICULTURAL SUB-ZONE KNOWN AS LOT NO. 309, CONTAINING AN AREA OF 17,259 SQUARE SQUARES, SITUATED AT BARANGAY BUENAVISTA, THIS CITY, TO RESIDENTIAL ZONE-1

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 2
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires the newly reclassified land to follow all city zoning rules and laws regarding its new residential use.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 3
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States that if any part of this law is found invalid, the rest of the law still applies.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 4

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 5

official_title: AN ORDINANCE RECLASSIFYING A PRODUCTION AGRICULTURAL SUB-ZONE KNOWN AS LOT NO. 361-A, CONTAINING AN AREA OF 50,736 SQUARE METERS, SITUATED AT BARANGAY GUISAO, THIS CITY, TO RESIDENTIAL ZONE-1

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 2
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires that the newly reclassified land must be used in accordance with the city's zoning laws and regulations.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 3
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States that if any part of this law is found invalid, the rest of the law still applies.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 4
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Cancels any older local rules that go against this new reclassification.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE PROVIDING FOR THE GENDER DEVELOPMENT CODE OF ZAMBOANGA CITY

articles_and_sections.title: Article I - Title, Policy, Principles, and Definition of Terms
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Establishes the name of the code and outlines the general policies on gender equality and defines key terms.

articles_and_sections.title: Article II - GAD Structure, Duties and Functions and its Seal
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Creates the Gender and Development Focal Point Committee and its technical working group to oversee gender programs.

articles_and_sections.title: Article III - Support Services for Women
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Mandates support services and protection programs for women survivors of violence and those in the entertainment industry.

articles_and_sections.title: Article IV - Public Participation of Women
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Promotes equal opportunities for women in government and community development activities.

articles_and_sections.title: Article V - Cultural Development
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Ensures access to education and alternative learning systems for indigenous and Muslim women.

articles_and_sections.title: Article VI - Labor and Employment
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Protects women workers' rights regarding wages, maternity leave, safe working conditions, and equal job opportunities.

articles_and_sections.title: Article VII - Women's Health Rights
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Provides healthcare programs, maternal care, and health facility upgrades specifically tailored for women.

articles_and_sections.title: Article VIII - Women's Education Rights
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Promotes gender-fair educational materials, scholarships, and gender sensitivity training in schools.

articles_and_sections.title: Article IX - Socio-Economic Benefits for Women
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Establishes livelihood programs and entrepreneurial training for disadvantaged women and marginalized groups.

articles_and_sections.title: Article X - Special Sectoral Concerns
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Provides advocacy and support for differently-abled, elderly, detained, and mentally ill women.

articles_and_sections.title: Article XI - Mass Media
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Encourages gender-sensitive media portrayals and regulates internet cafes to protect minors and prevent cyber pornography.

articles_and_sections.title: Article XII - Final Provisions
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Covers general legal clauses including separability, repealing, and effectivity of the code.

eli5_summary: This law makes sure that men and women are treated fairly and equally in Zamboanga City. It creates special groups to protect women's rights, healthcare, education, and jobs, while stopping violence and unfair treatment.
governing_agency: Gender and Development Focal Point Committee

amended_by_details.changes: Completely replaced and repealed by the 2022 Revised Gender and Development (GAD) Code.
Amends specific provisions, structures, committees, and definitions of the Gender Development Code of Zamboanga City.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 2

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 3

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 4

official_title: AN ORDINANCE DECLARING THE MONTH OF OCTOBER OF EVERY YEAR AS THE INDIGENOUS PEOPLES MONTH IN THE CITY OF ZAMBOANGA, CELEBRATING THE INDIGENOUS CULTURAL CUSTOMS, TRADITIONS AND PRACTICES AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS FOR THE PURPOSE

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 1. OFFICIAL DECLARATION
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Declares every October as Indigenous Peoples Month in Zamboanga City.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 2. CELEBRATION OF INDIGENOUS CULTURAL CUSTOMS, TRADITIONS, AND PRACTICES
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Lists out the different festivals, pageants, sports, and cultural events to be showcased during the month.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 3. IMPLEMENTATION
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Assigns the City Tourism Office and the IPMR to work together with local tribes to run the celebration.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 4. APPROPRIATION CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets aside 5 million pesos to fund the annual celebration.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 5. REPEALING CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Cancels any older rules that go against this new ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 6. SEPARABILITY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States that if one part of the law is found illegal, the rest of the law still stays active.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 7. EFFECTIVITY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Explains when the law officially starts working.

eli5_summary: Zamboanga City officially declared the month of October as Indigenous Peoples Month to celebrate the local tribes' culture and traditions. The city set aside 5 million pesos to fund fun events like festivals, pageants, and food fairs for everyone to enjoy.

amendment_details.changes: Repealed in its entirety, removing the renaming of Veterans Avenue to Assemblyman Joaquin F. Enriquez, Jr. Avenue.

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires the land to be used according to the city's zoning rules and laws.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 3

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 4

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 5

official_title: AN ORDINANCE NAMING THE EXISTING ROAD LEADING TO JOHN SPIRIG SR. MEMORIAL ELEMENTARY SCHOOL MORE PARTICULARLY DESCRIBED AS ROAD LOT 291-0, AT KAMPUNG ISLAM, THIS CITY AS “TEMOTEO ROJAS DRIVE”

articles_and_sections.title: Section 1 - Title
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section officially names the road leading to John Spirig Sr. Memorial Elementary School as 'Temoteo Rojas Drive'.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 2 - Effectivity

search_keywords: John Spirig Sr. Memorial Elementary School

official_title: AN ORDINANCE REORGANIZING THE ZAMBOANGA CITY DISASTER RISK REDUCTION AND MANAGEMENT OFFICE (ZCDRRMO), PROVIDING FOR ITS ORGANIZATIONAL STRUCTURE, FUNCTIONS AND PERSONNEL, APPROPRIATING FUNDS FOR ITS OPERATIONS, AND FOR OTHER RELATED PURPOSES
authors: Hon. Juan Climaco P. Elago II

articles_and_sections.title: Section 1. Title
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States the official name of the ordinance reorganizing the city's disaster office.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 2. Organizational Structure, Functions and Personnel
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Establishes the disaster office as a separate department with three divisions (Training, Planning, and Operations) and lists all their duties to protect the city from calamities.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 3. Staffing of the ZCDRRMO
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Explains the rules for hiring, reassigning, or detailing staff members to work in the disaster office.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 4. Separability Clause
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Ensures that if any part of this law is declared invalid, the remaining parts will still stay in effect.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 5. Repealing Clause
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Amends Ordinance No. 419 and replaces any older rules that go against this new ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 6. Effectivity Clause
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States that this law takes effect immediately.

eli5_summary: This law reorganizes Zamboanga City's disaster response team into an official department called the ZCDRRMO. It creates three divisions to handle training, risk planning, and early warnings or emergency responses. Its main job is to keep citizens safe, run emergency call networks, and help communities prepare for natural disasters.
governing_agency: Zamboanga City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (ZCDRRMO)

amendment_details.changes: Reorganizes the Zamboanga City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office and amends Ordinance No. 419 accordingly.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE ESTABLISHING FREE AND ACCESSIBLE GREEN CHILDREN’S PARK AND PLAYGROUND WITHIN THE BARANGAYS OF THE CITY OF ZAMBOANGA, DEFINING THE GUIDELINES, REGULATIONS, OPERATIONS AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREOF
authors: HON. ROLANDO DE VERA NAVARRO, JR.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 1. Short Title
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Names the law as the Green Children's Park and Playground Ordinance of Zamboanga City.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 2. Declaration of Policy
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets the rule that every child in Zamboanga should have access to safe, free, and nature-friendly parks.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 3. Objectives
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Lists goals like helping children play, bringing families together, and teaching them to care for nature.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 4. Definition of Terms
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Explains what a child, a green playground, playground facilities, and vandalism mean under this law.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 5. Establishment of Free and Accessible Green Children’s Park and Playground
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Orders the creation of eco-friendly parks for kids in all barangays, focusing on areas outside the city center first.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 6. Green Children’s Park and Playground Committee
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Creates a special team led by the Mayor and local officials to plan and manage the parks.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 7. Functions of the Committee
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Gives the committee the job of finding locations, making rules, and accepting donations for the parks.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 8. Supervision and Maintenance
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Makes barangays responsible for everyday care and safety, while the city handles major repairs.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 9. Operating Hours
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Gives barangays the power to set opening hours and bans school children from using the park during school hours.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 10. Community Involvement
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Invites community groups and organizations to help build and take care of the parks.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 11. Prohibited Acts
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Lists bad behaviors not allowed in the park, such as bullying, littering, smoking, vandalism, and bringing bikes or pets.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 12. Administrative Fines
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets cash fines and temporary or permanent bans for adults who break park rules.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 13. Appropriations
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets aside at least 10 million pesos to start building these parks.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 14. Repealing Clause
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Cancels any older rules that go against this new ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 15. Separability Clause

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 1. REORGANIZATION
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Reorganizes the city planning office into five separate divisions.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 3. PLANNING AND PROGRAMMING DIVISION
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Creates a division focused on land use and comprehensive development plans.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 4. RESEARCH, EVALUATION AND STATISTICS DIVISION
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Establishes a division to handle research, data gathering, and project monitoring.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 5. SPECIAL PROJECTS DIVISION
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets up a division to handle special development projects and fiscal policies.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 6. ZONING ADMINISTRATION DIVISION
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Creates a dedicated division just for enforcing zoning rules and issuing zoning permits.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 7. ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES DIVISION
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Provides general administrative support for the office.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 8. APPROPRIATION
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets aside funding and allows hiring for the new divisions.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 9. SEPARABILITY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Ensures that if one part of this law is found illegal, the rest still stays active.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 10. REPEALING CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Cancels older rules that go against this new ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 11. EFFECTIVITY
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States when this law officially takes effect.

eli5_summary: The city is splitting up its planning and zoning office into five smaller teams so they can do a better job managing city growth, building projects, and enforcing zoning rules. official_title: AN ORDINANCE REORGANIZING AND STRENGTHENING THE PUBLIC EMPLOYMENT SERVICE OFFICE (PESO) OF THE CITY OF ZAMBOANGA PURSUANT TO REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8759, AS AMENDED BY REPUBLIC ACT NO. 10691

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 1. TITLE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Names this law the Public Employment Service Office (PESO) Ordinance of the City of Zamboanga.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 2. DEFINITION OF TERMS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Defines words and abbreviations used throughout the ordinance so everyone understands the exact meanings.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 3. OBJECTIVES
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Lists the main goals of PESO, which include helping people find jobs quickly and sharing information about labor programs.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 4. DUTIES AND FUNCTIONS OF PESO
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Explains the specific jobs PESO does, like keeping job lists, helping match workers with employers, providing career advice, and supporting livelihood programs.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 5. OTHER SERVICES OF THE PESO
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Details extra programs PESO handles, such as job fairs, student work programs, anti-human trafficking efforts, and setting up barangay employment offices.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 6. ADMINISTRATIVE SUPERVISION AND STAFF COMPLEMENT
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Places PESO under the Mayor's office and sets up the official staffing positions and their specific duties.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 7. SUPPORT AND LINKAGES
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires PESO to work closely with national agencies like DOLE and TESDA, as well as local schools and offices.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 8. APPROPRIATION CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Ensures the city government will provide the necessary money to fund this office.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 9. TRANSITORY PROVISIONS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Gives the city two years to fully set up the new office, allowing the old setup to run things in the meantime.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 10. SEPARABILITY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States that if a court cancels one part of this law, the rest of the law stays safe and active.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 11. REPEALING CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Cancels any older rules that conflict with this new ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 12. EFFECTIVITY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets when this law officially takes effect according to the Local Government Code.

eli5_summary: Zamboanga City is upgrading and organizing its Public Employment Service Office (PESO) into its own dedicated division under the Mayor's office. This office will help people find jobs, provide career coaching, run job fairs, and support workers and students. official_title: AN ORDINANCE ESTABLISHING AND REGULATING NIGHT MARKET IN ZAMBOANGA CITY, PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF, ALLOCATING FUNDS FOR ITS OPERATIONS AND FOR OTHER RELATED PURPOSES

articles_and_sections.title: Article I - Preliminary Provisions
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets the official title, main goals, and definitions of terms used in the ordinance, including the operational hours and locations of the night market.

articles_and_sections.title: Article II - Administrative Provisions
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Creates a Night Market Committee to manage the market and details its duties, leadership, and staff.

articles_and_sections.title: Article III - Night Market Operations
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Outlines the nightly operating hours (6 PM to 12 MN), approved locations, allowed vendor sections, and traffic rules.

articles_and_sections.title: Article IV - The Concessionaires
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Lists the application requirements, rules on stall assignments, permits, and ID cards for vendors.

articles_and_sections.title: Article V - Installation, Display and Removal of Goods and Other Paraphernalia
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires vendors to keep displays within their designated spaces and use only lightweight, easily removable structures.

articles_and_sections.title: Article VI - Business Taxes, Regulatory and Other Fees
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets a rental fee of 10 pesos per square meter per night and requires payment of standard business and regulatory taxes.

articles_and_sections.title: Article VII - Duties, Responsibilities and Other Prohibitions
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets rules for cleanliness, waste disposal, and lists forbidden acts like selling alcohol, gambling, or subletting stalls.

articles_and_sections.title: Article VIII - Administrative Fines and Penal Clause
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Establishes fines ranging from 1,000 to 5,000 pesos for breaking the rules and allows for stall closures or legal charges.

articles_and_sections.title: Article IX - Appropriation Clause
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Allocates funding from existing city budgets for the night market operations.

articles_and_sections.title: Article X - Final Provisions
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Exempts the night market from standard zoning setback rules and ensures remaining rules stay valid if any part is found unconstitutional.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE INSTITUTIONALIZING AND PROMOTING URBAN AGRICULTURE IN ZAMBOANGA CITY, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREOF, AND FOR OTHER RELATED PURPOSES

articles_and_sections.title: Article I - Introductory Provision
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Establishes the official title of the law and outlines the general policies and definitions related to urban agriculture.

articles_and_sections.title: Article II - Use of Public and Private Open Spaces
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Encourages turning empty lots, subdivision spaces, school grounds, and household yards into food gardens, offering tax breaks for vacant land converted into farms.

articles_and_sections.title: Article III - Urban Garden Design
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Lists the different ways and places people can build urban gardens, such as on rooftops, walls, or in containers.

articles_and_sections.title: Article IV - Creation of the City Urban Agriculture Council
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Creates a special council led by the Mayor and local leaders to manage citywide urban farming programs, rules, and awards.

articles_and_sections.title: Article V - Biosafety, Urban Farming, and Planting Education Seminars
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Focuses on safe farming practices, teaching citizens how to garden, and running information campaigns.

articles_and_sections.title: Article VI - Urban Farming Technologies
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Promotes modern and eco-friendly farming methods like composting, recycling containers, hydroponics, and vertical planting.

articles_and_sections.title: Article VII - Research and Development
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Mandates research and master plans to constantly improve urban farming methods with help from schools and government agencies.

articles_and_sections.title: Article VIII - Households, Urban Barangays, Women and Youth, and Department of Education Participation
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires local barangays and schools to actively participate, budget for, and teach urban agriculture.

articles_and_sections.title: Article IX - Appropriation Clause
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets aside city funds to properly run the urban agriculture program.

articles_and_sections.title: Article X - Final Provision
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Ensures that if one part of the law is canceled, the rest stays active, and repeals any conflicting older rules.

eli5_summary: Zamboanga City is officially encouraging everyone to grow their own food in backyards, empty lots, schools, and rooftops. The city will provide seeds, training, and even tax breaks for landowners who turn empty spaces into green gardens to help feed the community and keep the environment clean.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE PROVIDING FOR THE PREVENTION PROGRAMS TO ADDRESS THE INCREASING ADOLESCENT PREGNANCY WITHIN THE TERRITORIAL JURISDICTION OF ZAMBOANGA CITY AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREOF

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 1. SHORT TITLE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Names the ordinance as the "Zamboanga City Ordinance on the Prevention of Adolescent Pregnancy."

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 2. DECLARATION OF POLICY
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Outlines the city's commitment to protecting youth rights, promoting reproductive health, and reducing adolescent pregnancy.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 3. DEFINITION OF TERMS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Defines key terms used throughout the ordinance, such as adolescents, comprehensive sexuality education, and adolescent friendly health services.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 4. ZAMBOANGA CITY ADOLESCENT PREGNANCY PREVENTION COUNCIL (ZCAPPC)
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Creates a special council to oversee and manage programs aimed at preventing adolescent pregnancy.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 5. DEVELOPMENT OF ZAMBOANGA CITY PROGRAM OF ACTION AND INVESTMENT PLAN FOR THE PREVENTION OF ADOLESCENT PREGNANCY (ZCPAIP-PAP)
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires the creation of a detailed action and investment plan to fight teenage pregnancy.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 6. INFORMATION AND SERVICE DELIVERY NETWORK FOR ADOLESCENT HEALTH DEVELOPMENT (ISDN FOR AHD)
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets up a network of organizations and facilities to provide health information and services to young people.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 7. CULTURALLY-SENSITIVE, AGE AND DEVELOPMENT APPROPRIATE COMPREHENSIVE SEXUALITY EDUCATION (CSE)
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Promotes age-appropriate education about reproductive health in schools and communities.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 8. ADOLESCENT FRIENDLY HEALTH SERVICES (AFHS) TRAINING FOR POLICY-MAKERS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires local leaders and policy-makers to receive training on adolescent health and rights.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 9. TRAINING OF TEACHERS, GUIDANCE COUNSELORS, SCHOOL SUPERVISORS, AND SCHOOL NURSES ON ADOLESCENT REPRODUCTIVE HEALTH CURRICULUM
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Ensures school staff are trained to properly guide and educate students on reproductive health.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 10. CSE FOR OUT-OF-SCHOOL ADOLESCENTS AND THOSE WITH SPECIAL CONCERNS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Extends reproductive health education to youth who are not in school or have special needs.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 11. DESIGNATED DAY FOR ADOLESCENT HEALTH AND DEVELOPMENT
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Establishes a dedicated day each week at health centers for youth to easily and confidentially access health services.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 12. MEDIA PARTICIPATION IN CSE PROMOTION
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Authorizes partnerships with private media to broadcast positive messages about youth health and sexuality.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 13. ACCESS TO REPRODUCTIVE HEALTH SERVICES
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Ensures minors can access family planning and maternal care with proper guidance, parental consent, and trained health providers.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 14. SOCIAL PROTECTION FOR ADOLESCENT MOTHERS OR PARENTS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Provides support systems like PhilHealth coverage, livelihood training, and maternal care for young parents to prevent repeat pregnancies.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 15. SOCIAL PROTECTION IN CASES OF SEXUAL VIOLENCE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Offers legal, medical, and psychological support for young mothers whose pregnancies resulted from sexual abuse.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 16. SOCIAL PROTECTION IN CASES OF HUMANITARIAN, ARMED CONFLICT, AND EMERGENCY SITUATIONS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Ensures adolescent health services continue even during crises, disasters, or armed conflicts.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 17. CARE AND MANAGEMENT FOR FIRST TIME PARENTS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Provides education and support classes for first-time teen parents regarding baby care and parenting.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 18. ENCOURAGING MALE INVOLVEMENT
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Creates programs to involve young men and boys in pregnancy prevention and responsible fatherhood.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 19. INTEGRATION OF LOCAL PROGRAMS FOR THE PREVENTION OF TEENAGE PREGNANCY IN SK PROGRAMS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires Sangguniang Kabataan (SK) funds and programs to support teenage pregnancy prevention activities.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 20. RESIDENTIAL CARE FACILITIES FOR DISADVANTAGED WOMEN
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Improves residential facilities to better accommodate and support pregnant teens.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 21. APPROPRIATION
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets aside an initial budget of Two Million Pesos (Php2,000,000.00) to carry out the ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 22. FINE AND PENALTIES FOR PROHIBITED ACTS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets fines and prison sentences for violating privacy, spreading misinformation, or denying health services to teens.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 23. IMPLEMENTING RULES
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Directs the newly created council to issue further rules for putting the ordinance into action.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 24. SUNSET REVIEW
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires a review of the ordinance after three years to see how well it is working.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 25. REPEALING CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Cancels any older rules that conflict with this new ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 26. SEPARABILITY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States that if one part of the law is found invalid, the rest remains in effect.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 27. EFFECTIVITY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Says when the ordinance officially becomes active.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 2. DECLARATION OF POLICY

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 3. DEFINITION OF TERMS

fines.penalty: P1,000.00 (Applies to transport violations, swill feeding, and mixed livestock/poultry raising)

eli5_summary: This law helps Zamboanga City protect animals and people from dangerous contagious diseases. official_title: THE SANITARY AND PHYTOSANITARY ORDINANCE FOR BORDER CONTROL POINTS IN ZAMBOANGA CITY

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets up border control points in major entry areas like Licomo and Limpapa to screen incoming agricultural products, aquatic items, wildlife, and people.

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Details the funding, budget appropriations, fee collections, and legal assistance for personnel involved in running the border control points.

fines.penalty: Five Thousand Pesos (PhP3,000.00) fine and confiscation of prohibited items.

eli5_summary: Zamboanga City is setting up checkpoints at major borders to inspect incoming animals, plants, food, and travelers to stop dangerous diseases from entering. If anyone brings in prohibited items or shows signs of a contagious illness, their goods will be confiscated and they may face fines or quarantine. This protects the local health, farming, and fishing industries.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE OF THE ENVIRONMENT CODE OF THE CITY OF ZAMBOANGA
co_authors: Hon. Juan Climaco P. Elago II

articles_and_sections.title: Article I - General Provisions
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Establishes the official title of the ordinance as the Environment Code and defines key environmental terms and policies.

articles_and_sections.title: Article II - Land Resources Management
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Outlines rules for managing land, forests, ancestral domains, and promoting organic agriculture.

articles_and_sections.title: Article III - Protected Areas and Biodiversity Conservation
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Focuses on protecting parks, wildlife, watersheds, caves, wetlands, mangroves, and ensuring animal welfare.

articles_and_sections.title: Article IV - Use and Development of Mineral Resources
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Reiterates the ban on large-scale mining in watersheds and regulates small-scale mining and quarrying.

articles_and_sections.title: Article V - Inland Water Management
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Protects freshwater sources from pollution, sets wastewater rules, and regulates deep wells.

articles_and_sections.title: Article VI - Air Quality Management
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Implements clean air standards, vehicle emission checks, smoking bans, and noise/odor controls.

articles_and_sections.title: Article VII - Ecotourism Development and Promotion
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Promotes sustainable eco-tourism and community-managed natural attractions.

articles_and_sections.title: Article VIII - Climate Change and Disaster Risk Reduction Management
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Integrates climate change adaptation and disaster preparedness into local plans.

articles_and_sections.title: Article IX - Culturally-Sensitive Populace and Human Settlements
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Ensures housing and settlement plans respect indigenous cultures, gender needs, and safety.

articles_and_sections.title: Article X - Waste Management and Sanitation Maintenance
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Mandates garbage segregation, proper healthcare waste disposal, sanitation, and bans toxic imported waste.

articles_and_sections.title: Article XI - Renewable and Alternative Energy Resources
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Encourages clean energy use like solar, wind, and waste-to-energy projects.

articles_and_sections.title: Article XII - Urban and Development and Green Design
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires green building practices, energy efficiency, open spaces, and proper parking layouts.

articles_and_sections.title: Article XIII - Integrated Fisheries and Coastal Resource Management and Development
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Protects municipal waters, marine protected areas, mangroves, and prioritizes local fisherfolk.

articles_and_sections.title: Article XIV - Environmental Impact Statement (EIS) System
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires major projects and businesses to undergo environmental impact checks before getting approval.

articles_and_sections.title: Article XV - Environmental Information and Education
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Promotes public awareness, education, and community participation in environmental protection.

articles_and_sections.title: Article XVI - Institutional Mechanisms
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Establishes local boards and councils to enforce environmental laws and manage resources.

articles_and_sections.title: Article XVII - Separability Clause
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Ensures that if one part of this law is found invalid, the rest remains active.

articles_and_sections.title: Article XVIII - Effectivity Clause
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States when the ordinance officially takes effect.

eli5_summary: Zamboanga City's comprehensive Environment Code sets clear rules to protect nature, clean the air and water, manage garbage properly, and keep the community safe. It covers everything from planting trees and protecting wildlife to green building designs and waste segregation. Everyone in the city must follow these rules to ensure a healthy and safe home for future generations.
governing_agency: Office of the City Environment and Natural Resources (OCENR)

official_title: AN ORDINANCE MANDATING BUSINESS ESTABLISHMENTS OPERATING WITHIN THE TERRITORIAL JURISDICTION IN THE CITY OF ZAMBOANGA TO INSTALL A CLOSED CIRCUIT TELEVISION (CCTV) SYSTEM AND PRESCRIBING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF
authors: HON. JUAN CLIMACO P. ELAGO II

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 1. TITLE OF ORDINANCE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Names the law as the CCTV mandate ordinance for Zamboanga City businesses.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 2. SCOPE AND APPLICATION
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Lists which types of businesses with high capitalization or sales must install working CCTV systems.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 3. PRESERVATION OF VIDEO FEEDS AND RECORDINGS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires business owners to keep their camera recordings for at least one week.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 4. MINIMUM TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets the minimum technical requirements for the cameras, recorders, and hard drives to ensure good video quality.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 5. INSTALLATION GUIDE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Provides recommendations on where to place cameras and store recording devices safely.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 6. MINIMUM COVERAGE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Tells businesses exactly which areas inside and outside their store must be covered by the cameras.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 7. IMPLEMENTING OFFICES
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Gives city offices the power to inspect businesses and verify they have working CCTVs before issuing business permits.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 8. NOTICE OF SURVEILLANCE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires businesses to put up a visible sign telling the public that the area is under CCTV surveillance.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 9. PROHIBITED SURVEILLANCE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Bans placing CCTV cameras in private areas like restrooms, toilets, and changing rooms.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 10. CONFIDENTIALITY AND NON-DISCLOSURE OF VIDEO RECORDINGS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Mandates that businesses must protect the privacy of recorded footage under the Data Privacy Act.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 11. ALLOWED USE DISCLOSURE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Lists the few specific cases where CCTV footage can be viewed or shared, mainly for law enforcement and legal investigations.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 12. PENALTIES
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States that businesses without working CCTVs cannot get a business permit and will face a fine of 5,000 pesos per day until fixed.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 13. APPEAL PROCESS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Explains how a business can appeal a violation finding to the Mayor's office within five days.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 14. SEPARABILITY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States that if one part of this law is found invalid, the rest of the law still applies.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 15. REPEALING CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Cancels any older rules that conflict with this new CCTV ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 16. EFFECTIVITY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets the ordinance to fully take effect two years after its approval.

fines.penalty: PHP 5,000.00 fine per day that the violation continues, plus denial of business permit.

eli5_summary: Certain large businesses in Zamboanga City must install and maintain working CCTV cameras to help prevent and solve crimes. These cameras must record clearly, cover specific areas like entrances and cashiers, and respect people's privacy. Businesses that fail to follow this rule will face fines and will not receive their business permits.
governing_agency: Business Permits and Licensing Office (BPLO) and Computer Services Division (CSD)

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 6. REPEALING CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Cancels any older rules that conflict with this ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 7. EFFECTIVITY CLAUSE

eli5_summary: If you are behind on your property taxes from 2020 or earlier, the city is giving you a break by forgiving your extra penalties and interest. You just need to pay before the end of December 2020, as long as your property isn't already tied up in legal or auction processes.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE ADOPTING R.A. 9165 OTHERWISE KNOWN AS “COMPREHENSIVE DANGEROUS DRUGS ACT OF 2002” AND CREATING ZAMBOANGA CITY DANGEROUS DRUGS BOARD (ZCDDB) AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREOF
co_authors: HON. JUAN CLIMACO P. ELAGO II

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 1. TITLE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Names this rulebook the Zamboanga City Dangerous Drug Board (ZCDDB) ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 2. DECLARATION OF POLICY
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States the city's goal to protect people, especially youth, from dangerous drugs and help victims recover.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 3. PURPOSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets up a team to create plans and stop drug abuse in the city.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 4. DEFINITION OF TERMS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Explains special words used in the ordinance so everyone understands them clearly.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 5. UNLAWFUL ACTS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Lists all the illegal actions related to dangerous drugs, like selling, using, or making them.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 6. PARTICIPATION OF FAMILY, STUDENTS, TEACHERS AND SCHOOL AUTHORITIES IN ENFORCEMENT OF THIS ORDINANCE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Explains how families and schools must teach kids about the dangers of drugs and include it in lessons.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 7. HEADS, SUPERVISORS, AND TEACHER OF SCHOOLS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Gives school leaders the power to report or stop drug violations happening at school.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 8. ABATEMENT OF DRUG RELATED PUBLIC NUISANCES
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Declares any place used to sell or deliver illegal drugs a public nuisance.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 9. PROCEDURE IN THE ABATEMENT OF DRUG RELATED PUBLIC NUISANCES
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Explains how the city can investigate and shut down places used for illegal drugs.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 10. EFFECT OF BOARD DECLARATION
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Allows the board to close down dangerous drug dens for up to a year.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 11. CREATION OF ZAMBOANGA CITY DANGEROUS DRUG BOARD OR (ZCDDB)
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Creates the special board made of city officials and community leaders to fight drug abuse.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 12. DUTIES AND FUNCTIONS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Tells the board members how often to meet and what tasks they need to do to stop drugs.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 13. FORMULATION OF IMPLEMENTING RULES AND REGULATIONS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Gives the board one month to write down the detailed rules for this ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 14. APPROPRIATIONS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets aside money from the city budget to fund the anti-drug board's programs.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 15. SEPARABILITY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Ensures that if one part of this law is canceled, the rest still stays active.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 16. REPEALING CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Cancels any older city rules that go against this new law.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 17. EFFECTIVITY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Says this law becomes active right after it is published for everyone to see.

eli5_summary: Zamboanga City adopted the national anti-drug law and created a special board to fight illegal drugs. This board works with schools, families, and police to stop drug use, shut down drug dens, and help people recover. The city also set aside money to fund these anti-drug programs.

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This ordinance is officially called the 'Green Ordinance'.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 2 - Appropriation
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: The city sets aside 500,000 pesos every year for four years to buy fruit tree seedlings.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 3 - Distribution of Seedlings
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: The city will give these seedlings to residents living at least 5 kilometers away from City Hall.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 4 - Obligations of Beneficiaries
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: People who receive trees must plant and care for them, pay back the cost of the seedlings once they bear fruit, and help share more seedlings with others later.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 6 - Supervision and Administration
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: A 'Green Committee' is created to manage the program and choose who gets the seedlings.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 8 - Qualification of Beneficiaries
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: To get seedlings, you must live in the area for at least two years, own the land where you will plant, and agree to follow the program's rules.

eli5_summary: The city is spending money to buy fruit tree seedlings to give to farmers and residents living outside the city center. In return, the people who get the trees must take good care of them and eventually pay back the cost of the seedlings once the trees start producing fruit.

official_title: AN ENABLING ORDINANCE ON THE PROMOTION OF BREASTFEEDING IN THE WORKPLACE AND PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREOF

articles_and_sections.title: Section 1 - Title
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section names the law as the Promotion of Breastfeeding in the Workplace and Providing Penalties Thereof.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 2 - Declaration of Policy
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: The city wants to support breastfeeding mothers by creating safe and healthy environments at work.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 3 - Definition of Terms
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section explains what specific words like 'lactation station' and 'nursing employee' mean in this law.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 4 - Scope/Applicability
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This law applies to all private businesses and government offices in Zamboanga City.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 5 - Establishment of Lactation Stations
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Employers must provide a clean, private, and comfortable room for mothers to breastfeed or pump milk.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 6 - Lactation Periods
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Nursing mothers are allowed extra breaks during the workday to breastfeed or express milk.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 7 - Access to Breastfeeding Information
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Employers must teach pregnant employees about the benefits of breastfeeding and how to continue it after returning to work.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 8 - Incentives and Awards System
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: The City Health Office will create a way to reward businesses that follow this law.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 9 - Breastfeeding Awareness Month
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: August is officially designated as Breastfeeding Awareness Month.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 10 - Implementation and Monitoring
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: A special team led by the City Health Office will check if businesses are following the rules.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 11 - Penalties
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Businesses that do not follow the rules will face fines and could lose their business permits.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 12 - Funding
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: The city will use money from the Gender and Development Fund to pay for this program.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 13 - Separability Clause
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: If one part of this law is found to be invalid, the rest of the law still stays in effect.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 14 - Effectivity Clause
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This law starts working according to the rules in the Local Government Code.

fines.penalty: P1,000.00 plus warning to be issued by the City Health Office
P2,000.00 and non-extension of sanitary permit
P5,000.00 and the cancellation or revocation of business permits or licenses to operate

eli5_summary: This law requires all workplaces in Zamboanga City to provide a clean, private space for nursing mothers to breastfeed or pump milk. It also gives mothers extra break time to do this and sets penalties for businesses that do not provide these facilities.

articles_and_sections.title: Rule I - The Members

articles_and_sections.title: Rule II - The Presiding Officer

articles_and_sections.title: Rule III - The Secretary

articles_and_sections.title: Rule IV - Other Officers
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This allows the council to create additional leadership roles like a Floor Leader to help manage the flow of business.

articles_and_sections.title: Rule V - Committees and Committee Reports

articles_and_sections.title: Rule VI - Meetings and Quorum

articles_and_sections.title: Rule VII - Order of Business
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This sets the standard schedule for how meetings are run, from the opening prayer to the final adjournment.

articles_and_sections.title: Rule VIII - Procedure for Ordinances, Resolutions and Other Legislative Matters
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This explains the step-by-step process for turning a proposal into an official city law.

articles_and_sections.title: Rule IX - The Minutes
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This requires the council to keep an accurate written record of everything that happens during their meetings.

articles_and_sections.title: Rule X - Debates and Decorum
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This sets the rules for how members should behave and speak during meetings to ensure respectful and orderly discussions.

articles_and_sections.title: Rule XI - Votes and Voting
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This explains how members cast their votes on proposals and what happens if there is a tie.

articles_and_sections.title: Rule XII - Rules on Motions
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This provides a list of formal actions members can take to manage the flow of debate, such as pausing a discussion or ending a meeting.

articles_and_sections.title: Rule XIII - Unfinished Business at the End of the Session
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This ensures that any work not finished during a meeting is carried over to the next one.

articles_and_sections.title: Rule XIV - Papers and Documents
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This mandates that all official documents must be safely stored and made available to the public upon request.

articles_and_sections.title: Rule XV - Suspension of Rules
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This explains the rare circumstances under which the council can temporarily set aside their own rules.

articles_and_sections.title: Rule XVI - Amendments to Rules
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This outlines how the council can change these rules in the future if needed.

articles_and_sections.title: Rule XVII - Supplementary Rules
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This states that if these rules don't cover a situation, the council will follow standard parliamentary procedures.

articles_and_sections.title: Rule XVIII - Date of Effectivity
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This confirms when these rules officially started being used.

eli5_summary: This ordinance sets the 'rulebook' for how the Zamboanga City Council conducts its meetings. It explains how members should behave, how they vote on new laws, how committees work, and how the public can expect the council to operate.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE PROVIDING PROTECTION, SECURITY AND ASSISTANCE TO WHISTLEBLOWERS OF CERTAIN CRIMES COMMITTED BY OFFICIALS AND EMPLOYEES IN THE CITY GOVERNMENT OF ZAMBOANGA AND FOR OTHER RELATED PURPOSES

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 1. TITLE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Names the ordinance as the Whistleblower Ordinance in City Government of Zamboanga.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 2. DEFINITION
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Defines key terms such as illegal acts, probable cause, public official or employee, retaliatory action, and whistleblower.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 3. WHISTLEBLOWER PROGRAM
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Establishes that anyone who has knowledge of illegal acts by city employees can apply for protection and benefits.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 4. ADMISSION TO THE PROGRAM
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Lists the rules a whistleblower must meet to join the program, such as making a sworn statement and keeping the matter confidential.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 5. WHISTLEBLOWER COMMITTEE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Creates a committee consisting of local prosecutors, police, and NBI officials to manage and evaluate whistleblower cases.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 6. WHISTLEBLOWER’S CONFIDENTIALITY; AND ITS PROCEEDINGS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Protects the identity of the whistleblower and penalizes anyone who leaks their name.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 7. PROTECTION AND SECURITY AGAINST DISCIPLINARY ACTION AND/OR REPRISAL ON WHISTLEBLOWER
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Grants immunity from lawsuits and provides security or enrollment in the witness protection program if needed.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 8. LIMITATIONS ON THE NUMBER OF WHISTLEBLOWERS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Limits the main whistleblowers in a case to a maximum of two if their testimonies are corroborative.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 9. RETALIATORY ACTIONS AGAINST A WHISTLEBLOWER
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Penalizes anyone who harms, threatens, or retaliates against a whistleblower or their family.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 10. RETALIATORY ACTIONS AGAINST A WHISTLEBLOWER IN THE WORKPLACE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Penalizes workplace bullying, unfair performance reviews, or demotions directed at a whistleblower.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 11. DISCRIMINATORY HIRING
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Makes it illegal for any company or government office to reject a job applicant just because they are a whistleblower.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 12. FALSE, MISLEADING OR MALICIOUS DISCLOSURES
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Punishes people who lie or make fake reports just to harass someone, and pauses the program during election years.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 13. FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE TO A WHISTLEBLOWER
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Provides a cash assistance of 100,000 pesos to qualified whistleblowers given in two parts.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 14. APPROPRIATION CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets aside at least one million pesos in the city budget to fund the whistleblower program and rewards.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 15. SEPARABILITY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Ensures that if one part of this law is found invalid, the rest of the law still works.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 16. REPEALING CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Cancels any older city rules that go against this ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 17. EFFECTIVITY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States when the ordinance officially takes effect according to local government rules.

fines.penalty: Imprisonment of six (6) months to one (1) year and a fine of Five Thousand Pesos (Php5,000.00)
fines.offense_level: Violation by investigating officer leaking identity / Retaliation / Discriminatory hiring / False disclosures

eli5_summary: This law protects and rewards city employees or citizens who step forward to report corruption or crimes committed by Zamboanga City government workers. It keeps their identity secret, protects them from losing their jobs or facing retaliation, and gives them financial help if they help successfully prosecute the wrongdoers.
governing_agency: Whistleblower Committee (Regional State Prosecutor IX, NBI Regional Director, Zamboanga City Police Director)

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Disco houses cannot be built within 50 meters of City Hall, schools, churches, or hospitals.

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: The owner must keep the place safe, prevent illegal activities, and ensure no indecent dancing occurs.

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Owners must provide security and ensure no alcohol is sold to anyone under 21.

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: The City Mayor is in charge of checking that disco houses follow these rules.

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Owners must get a business permit and health permit before opening.

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: If the rules are broken, the city can temporarily close the disco or take away its business license.

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Citizens can report disco houses that are in the wrong place or breaking the law to the Mayor.

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Allows courts to issue fines up to 5,000 Pesos or up to a year in jail for severe rule violations.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE AMENDING CERTAIN PROVISIONS OF ORDINANCE NO. 413, SERIES OF 2013, ENTITLED “AN ORDINANCE REGULATING SMOKING IN THE CITY OF ZAMBOANGA AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF”
co_authors: HON. JUAN CLIMACO P. ELAGO II

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 1. TITLE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Names this law as the smoking regulation ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 2. PURPOSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Outlines the goals of protecting public health, promoting clean environments, and keeping tobacco away from minors.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 3. COVERAGE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States that smoking is banned in all enclosed public places, workplaces, and public transportation unless inside an approved smoking area.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 4. DEFINITION OF TERMS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Defines key terms used in the ordinance such as smoking, e-cigarettes, public places, minors, and designated smoking areas.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 5. PROHIBITED ACTS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Lists unlawful acts, including smoking in prohibited places, selling tobacco to minors, or selling tobacco products near schools.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 6. DESIGNATED SMOKING AREA AND NON-SMOKING AREA
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets strict physical and ventilation standards that businesses must follow if they want to build a legal smoking area.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 7. SALE OF TOBACCO PRODUCTS AND E-CIGARETTES WITHIN SCHOOL PERIMETERS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Bans the sale or distribution of tobacco and e-cigarettes within 100 meters of schools and playgrounds.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 8. DUTIES AND OBLIGATIONS OF PERSONS-IN-CHARGE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires business owners and administrators to post clear no-smoking signs, remove ashtrays, and stop violators.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 9. PERSONS LIABLE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Identifies who can be held responsible and punished when a violation occurs, including smokers, drivers, and business managers.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 10. ENFORCEMENT
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Creates a Smoke-Free Enforcement Team involving the mayor, police, and various city offices to implement the law.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 11. SMOKING CESSATION PROGRAM
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Establishes a program to help people who want to quit smoking.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 12. PENALTIES
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets out fines and community service hours for individuals and businesses caught breaking the rules.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 13. CITATION TICKETS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Authorizes police and enforcers to issue tickets to violators.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 14. FUNDING
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Allocates an initial budget of 500,000 pesos to fund the implementation of the ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 15. DEPUTIZED OFFICER
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Authorizes trained officers to monitor compliance and issue tickets.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 16. TRAINING AND DEPUTATION
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires all enforcers to pass training before receiving deputation from the mayor.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 17. POSTING OF BILLBOARD
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Orders the City Engineer's Office to put up public warning billboards.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 18. REPEALING CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Cancels older rules that contradict this ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 19. SEPARABILITY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Ensures the rest of the law stays valid even if one part is declared illegal.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 20. EFFECTIVITY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets when the ordinance officially takes effect.

fines.penalty: P1,000.00 fine or 2 hours of immediate community service cleaning the public place
P3,000.00 fine or 3 hours of immediate community service cleaning the public place
P5,000.00 fine or 5 hours of immediate community service cleaning the public place

eli5_summary: This law bans smoking and vaping in all enclosed public places, workplaces, and public transportation in Zamboanga City to protect people from second-hand smoke. It sets strict rules for businesses, bans selling tobacco products near schools and to minors, and imposes fines or community service for violators.

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets the new tricycle fare to 35 pesos for the first one or two passengers for the first kilometer, plus 10 pesos for a third passenger, and 10 pesos for every extra kilometer.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 2 - Repealing Clause
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Cancels any old rules or orders that go against this new fare adjustment.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 3 - Separability Clause
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Ensures that if one part of this law is found illegal, the rest of the rules still stay in effect.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 4 - Effectivity Clause
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States when this new law officially starts following government rules.

eli5_summary: This new law changes how much tricycle drivers can charge for rides in Zamboanga City because fuel prices went up. Now, the starting fare is 35 pesos for one or two passengers for the first kilometer, with extra charges for a third passenger or for extra distance.

amendment_details.changes: Updates Section 1 (a) of Article V to change the official tricycle fare rates due to rising fuel costs and inflation.
