official_title: AN ORDINANCE GRANTING TAX RELIEF AND/OR AMNESTY TO DELINQUENT REAL PROPERTY OWNERS FROM THE PAYMENT OF PENALTIES, SURCHARGES AND INTERESTS ON UNPAID REAL PROPERTY TAXES FROM THE PERIOD COVERING JANUARY 1, 2005 TO DECEMBER 31, 2010 AND FIFTY PERCENT (50%) TAX RELIEF ON PENALTIES, SURCHARGES AND INTERESTS COVERING THE PERIOD FROM JANUARY 1, 2000 TO DECEMBER 31, 2004

articles_and_sections.title: Section 1 - Title
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section names the law the 'Real Property Tax Relief and/or Amnesty Ordinance of 2011'.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 2 - Coverage
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section explains that property owners can get relief from penalties on unpaid taxes from 2005-2010, and a 50% discount on penalties for unpaid taxes from 2000-2004.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 3 - Exceptions
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section lists specific properties that cannot get this tax relief, such as those already under legal action or auction.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 4 - Duration
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section sets a deadline of December 15, 2011, for property owners to apply for this tax relief.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 5 - Moratorium
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section states that there will be no more tax amnesty programs for the next five years after this one.

eli5_summary: If you haven't paid your property taxes for certain years between 2000 and 2010, the city is giving you a chance to pay them without the extra penalty fees. You must apply for this help by December 15, 2011, to take advantage of the deal.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE AMENDING SECTIONS 8, 8.1, 8.1.1, 8.1.2, AND 8.1.3, OF ORDINANCE NO. 342, SERIES OF 2008, ENTITLED “AN ORDINANCE DEFINING THE GUIDELINES, REGULATIONS AND USE OF JARDIN MARIA CLARA L. official_title: AN ORDINANCE AUTHORIZING THE REORGANIZATION OF THE CITY GOVERNMENT OF ZAMBOANGA AS A HIGHLY URBANIZED CITY PURSUANT TO CIRCULAR No. 83-29, DATED DECEMBER 6, 1983, OF THE MINISTRY OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT

articles_and_sections.title: Section 1

articles_and_sections.title: Section 2

articles_and_sections.title: Section 3

eli5_summary: This law was created to update how the Zamboanga city government works after it was officially recognized as a big, busy city. It allows the Mayor to form a team to organize the city's offices and staff properly.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE REGULATING THE ESTABLISHMENT, CONSTRUCTION, EXPANSION, OPERATION AND PROLIFERATION OF PORTS, WHARVES, PIERS, FISH AND/OR BEACH LANDINGS, FINGER/MINI WHARVES, SHIPYARDS AND OTHER SIMILAR STRUCTURES IN Zamboanga CITY, PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF AND FOR OTHER RELATED PURPOSES
authors: HON. JUAN CLIMACO P. ELAGO II

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 1. TITLE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Names the law as the Ports, Wharves, Piers, Fish and/or Beach Landings, Finger/Mini Wharves, Shipyards and Other Similar Structures Regulatory Ordinance of the City of Zamboanga.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 2. DEFINITION OF TERMS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Defines important words used in the ordinance such as port, pier, wharf, drydock, and foreshore land so everyone understands what they mean.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 3. AUTHORITY OF AGENCIES
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Outlines the powers that different government groups like the PPA, DENR, MARINA, and the City have over coastal structures.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 4. PANTALAN INTER-AGENCY COMMITTEE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Creates a special team led by the City Mayor to check and evaluate all port and pier applications as a one-stop shop.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 5. POWERS AND FUNCTIONS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Gives the Inter-Agency Committee the power to review port applications, issue 'no objection' recommendations, and take down illegal structures.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 6. SECRETARIAT
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets up a secretariat to handle meetings, paperwork, and records for the Inter-Agency Committee.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 7. LICENSING, REGISTRATION OR ACCREDITATION AND ISSUANCE OF CERTIFICATION OF NO OBJECTION
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires anyone building a port or wharf to get proper licenses from authorized agencies and a 'no objection' clearance from the committee.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 8. EXISTING ILLEGAL STRUCTURES
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Orders that all illegal ports and piers found by the task force must be removed or torn down by their owners at their own expense.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 9. PROHIBITED ACTS OR OMISSION
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Makes it illegal to build or run a port, pier, or shipyard without proper permits, fail to tear down illegal structures, or lack a business permit.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 10. PENAL CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets fines and jail time for people who violate the rules by building illegal ports or failing to get business permits.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 11. PERSONS LIABLE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States that both individuals and company officials (like presidents or managers) can be held responsible if their organization breaks this law.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 12. SEPARABILITY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Ensures that if one part of this law is found invalid, the rest of the law will still stay in effect.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 13. REPEALING CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Cancels any older rules or ordinances that go against what this new ordinance says.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 14. EFFECTIVITY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Says this law takes effect right after it is published in a local newspaper.

fines.penalty: Imprisonment of one (1) year and a fine of Php5,000.00, plus demolition costs.
Imprisonment of six (6) months to one (1) year and a fine of Php5,000.00.

eli5_summary: This ordinance strictly regulates building and running ports, wharves, piers, and shipyards in Zamboanga City to stop illegal activities like smuggling. Anyone wanting to build or operate these structures must get proper permits and approval from a special Inter-Agency Committee. Any illegal ports or piers must be torn down by their owners, and violators face fines and jail time.

official_title: AN ENABLING ORDINANCE ESTABLISHING THE PREVENTION AND CONTROL OF HIGHLY COMMUNICABLE DISEASES WITH PUBLIC HEALTH IMPACT IN ZAMBOANGA CITY
co_authors: HON. JUAN CLIMACO P. ELAGO II

articles_and_sections.title: Section 1 - Title
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section names the ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 2 - Declaration of Policy
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: The city promises to protect people from dangerous diseases that spread easily.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 3 - Definition of Terms
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section lists the specific dangerous diseases and terms covered by this law.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 4 - Creation of Multi-Agency Task Force
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This creates a special group of leaders and health workers to manage disease outbreaks.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 5 - Duties
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Residents and medical workers must report suspected cases of dangerous diseases.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 6 - Quarantine of Persons
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: People who are sick or exposed to dangerous diseases must stay in isolation until they are cleared by doctors.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 7 - Other Preventive Measures
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section outlines extra safety steps like cleaning, public education, and rules for hospitals and funeral homes.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 8 - Funding
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: The city sets aside one million pesos to pay for these health programs.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 9 - Sanctions
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section explains the fines and punishments for breaking these health rules.

fines.penalty: Reprimand
Fine of P1,000.00 per unreported case
Fine of P2,000.00 - P3,000.00 per unreported case
Fine of P5,000.00 per unreported case
Revocation of license
Fine not exceeding P5,000.00 or imprisonment not exceeding 6 months, or both
Fine of P5,000.00 per person per act

eli5_summary: This law helps Zamboanga City stop the spread of dangerous diseases. It creates a special team to watch for sickness, requires people to report cases, and forces sick individuals to stay in quarantine to keep everyone else safe.

amendment_details.changes: Repealed Ordinance No. 7, series of 1976 in its entirety, which had amended Sections 2 and 3 of Ordinance No. 1721, series of 1975.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 8. EFFECTIVITY CLAUSE

official_title: AN ORDINANCE INITIATING THE CONVERSION OF RIO HONDO ELEMENTARY SCHOOL INTO RIO HONDO INTEGRATED SCHOOL AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR FOR ITS PERSONNEL AND INFRASTRUCTURE, AND OTHER PURPOSES

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 1. TITLE

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 4. LGU ASSISTANCE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets aside at least 50 million pesos from the city to build new classrooms and help run the school.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 5. REPEALING CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Cancels any older city rules that conflict with this new school conversion law.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 6. SEPARABILITY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Ensures that if one part of this law is found invalid, the rest of the law stays in effect.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 7. EFFECTIVITY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States that this law takes effect right after it is published in a newspaper.

eli5_summary: The city is turning Rio Hondo Elementary School into a bigger school that also teaches high school students. The city is giving at least 50 million pesos to build new classrooms so local kids can go to high school right in their neighborhood.
governing_agency: Department of Education / City Government of Zamboanga

official_title: AN ORDINANCE ESTABLISHING A BARANGAY HIGH SCHOOL AT TOLOSA, ZAMBOANGA CITY, AND PROVIDING APPROPRIATION THEREFOR

articles_and_sections.title: Section 2 - Site

articles_and_sections.title: Section 4 - Maintenance and Operating Expenses
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section ensures the city will provide money every year to keep the school running.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 6 - Teaching Staff and Other Allied Support

articles_and_sections.title: Section 7 - Authority for the Operation of the High School

official_title: AN ORDINANCE ADOPTING THE CITY OF ZAMBOANGA’S POWER AND ENERGY CODE TO PROMOTE ENERGY EFFICIENCY AND CONSERVATION, FACILITATE THE IMPLEMENTATION OF ENERGY PROJECTS, HARMONIZE LOCAL AND NATIONAL POLICIES ON ENERGY UTILIZATION, EFFICIENCY, SAFETY, RESILIENCE, AND DEVELOPMENT, AND FOR SUCH OTHER RELATED PURPOSES, AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR

articles_and_sections.title: Chapter I - Preliminary Provisions
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets the name of the law as the Local Power and Energy Code of Zamboanga and defines key terms related to energy efficiency.

articles_and_sections.title: Chapter II - Energy Sector Committee
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Creates a special committee led by the Mayor to oversee local energy projects and policies.

articles_and_sections.title: Chapter III - Energy Development
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Encourages exploring renewable energy sources and includes energy plans in city development maps.

articles_and_sections.title: Chapter IV - Power Distribution Development
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Aims for total household electricity and prevents activities that block power lines.

articles_and_sections.title: Chapter V - Energy Permits Regulatory Reforms
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Streamlines and speeds up the process for getting permits for energy projects.

articles_and_sections.title: Chapter VI - Downstream Oil Facilities
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Helps shut down illegal gas stations and freezes prices for cooking gas during emergencies.

articles_and_sections.title: Chapter VII - Energy Efficiency and Conservation
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Creates a new office to audit energy use and promote power-saving habits in government and businesses.

articles_and_sections.title: Chapter VIII - Transportation
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Promotes electric vehicles, alternative fuels, and charging stations in the city.

articles_and_sections.title: Chapter IX - Private Sector Participation
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Invites private businesses to invest in local energy and conservation projects.

articles_and_sections.title: Chapter X - Environmental Management
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Ensures all energy projects follow environmental laws and properly manage waste.

articles_and_sections.title: Chapter XI - Resiliency
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires energy facilities and businesses to prepare disaster plans to keep power running during emergencies.

articles_and_sections.title: Chapter XII - Information, Education, and Communication Campaign
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Spreads awareness about energy safety, conservation, and adds it to school lessons.

articles_and_sections.title: Chapter XIII - Awards and Citations
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Gives rewards and recognition to citizens and businesses that practice great energy conservation.

articles_and_sections.title: Chapter XIV - Final Provisions
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Provides funding, handles legal separation of clauses, and repeals conflicting rules.

eli5_summary: Zamboanga City created a new rule book to save electricity, use more renewable energy like solar or wind, and speed up building permits for power projects. It also promotes electric vehicles, sets up a team to manage energy emergencies, and rewards people who save power.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE BANNING THE TAKING OR CATCHING, SELLING AND TRANSPORTING OF SABALO (FULL GROWN BANGUS OR MILKFISH) AND PROVIDING PENALTY THEREOF

articles_and_sections.title: Section 1 - Definition of Terms
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section defines what 'sabalo' (large milkfish), catching, selling, and transporting mean for the purpose of this law.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 2 - Prohibition
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: It is illegal for anyone to catch, sell, or move sabalo in Zamboanga City, and business owners caught selling them will lose their permits.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 3 - Enforcement
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Local officials, police, and fishery officers are authorized to catch people breaking this law and take away the fish as evidence.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 4 - Penalties
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Breaking this law can result in a fine of up to 5,000 pesos, up to one year in jail, or both, and the fish will be taken away.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 5 - Effectivity
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This law starts working as soon as it is approved.

fines.penalty: Fine not exceeding P5,000.00 or imprisonment not exceeding 1 year or both

eli5_summary: This law protects large milkfish (sabalo) in Zamboanga City by making it illegal to catch, sell, or transport them. If you break this rule, you could face a fine or jail time, and any fish you have will be taken away.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE PROVIDING FOR PRESCRIBED MAINTENANCE MEDICINES AND/OR VITAMIN SUPPLEMENTS TO INDIGENT SENIOR CITIZENS-SUPPLEMENTING THE PHILIPPINE HEALTH INSURANCE CORPORATION’S (PHILHEALTH’S) KONSULTASYONG SULIT AT TAMA/YAMAN NG KALUSUGAN/GUARANTEED AND ACCESSIBLE MEDICATIONS FOR OUTPATIENT TREATMENT (KONSULTA/YAKAP/GAMOT) PROGRAM, IN SUPPORT OF THE UNIVERSAL HEALTH CARE ACT, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER RELATED PURPOSES

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 1. TITLE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This names the law the 'Largo Vida Ordinance of the City of Zamboanga'.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 2. DECLARATION OF POLICY
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: The city promises to protect health and help poor senior citizens get free medicine.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 3. OBJECTIVES
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: The goals are to give free medicine and vitamins to poor seniors and make health centers better.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 4. DEFINITION OF TERMS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This explains what words like indigent, maintenance medicine, and health stations mean in this law.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 5. SCOPE AND COVERAGE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This program covers poor senior citizens who have heart diseases, diabetes, lung problems, or degenerative illnesses.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 6. ELIGIBILITY
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: To join, you must have lived in Zamboanga for 10 years, be proven poor by a social worker, be registered at a health center, and have a covered sickness.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 7. REGISTRATION
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Seniors must bring IDs, a doctor's prescription, and an indigency certificate to sign up at the barangay.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 8. PROCEDURE FOR AVAILMENT
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Seniors must get check-ups every three months, sign up with PhilHealth Konsulta, get a digital ID, and claim their monthly medicine.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 9. COVERAGE OF MEDICINES AND SUPPLEMENTS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Approved medicines and vitamins for the four covered diseases will be provided and funded with help from PhilHealth.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 10. ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORDS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: The city health office will keep computer records of all patients and medicine supplies while keeping information private.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 11. ACCREDITATION OF DISTRICT HEALTH CENTERS AND BARANGAY HEALTH STATIONS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: All health centers must try to become official PhilHealth Konsulta clinics.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 12. LARGO VIDA BARANGAY HEALTH WORKERS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Special health workers will be hired and trained to help run health desks, process claims, and deliver medicines to bedridden seniors.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 13. LARGO VIDA WATCHGROUP
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: A local team in each barangay will check if applicants are truly poor and watch over the program's progress.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 14. LARGO VIDA HEALTH DAY
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Every second and fourth Friday of the month, health stations will prioritize seniors for check-ups and giving out medicines.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 15. DELIVERY OF LARGO VIDA MEDICINES AND SUPPLEMENTS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Medicines will be regularly delivered to health stations and brought straight to the homes of seniors who cannot walk or leave their houses.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 16. OVERSIGHT
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: The city council's committee on health will check regularly to make sure the program is working properly.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 17. APPROPRIATION CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: The city sets aside 50 million pesos starting in 2026 to buy medicines and pay for the program.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 18. REPEALING CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Old rules that go against this new law are changed or cancelled.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 19. SEPARABILITY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: If one part of this law is found illegal, the rest of the law still stays active.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 20. EFFECTIVITY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This law starts working right after it is published in a local newspaper.

eli5_summary: The Zamboanga City government is launching a special program to give free daily maintenance medicines and vitamins to poor senior citizens who suffer from illnesses like diabetes and heart disease. Health workers will help sign them up, give them digital IDs, and even deliver medicines straight to their homes if they cannot walk to the clinic.

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Establishes the structure, powers, and duties of the Office of the City Veterinarian, including its divisions and seven field offices across the city's barangays.

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Regulates slaughterhouses, meat markets, and meat transport to ensure all meat sold to the public is clean, safe, and properly inspected.

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires all dogs and cats to be vaccinated against rabies annually and outlines rules for pet registration, biting incidents, and stray animal control.

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Establishes the city pound to catch and impound stray animals roaming in public spaces.

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Allows the Department of Education to decide teacher numbers while the city helps fund operations.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 6. Repealing Clause

articles_and_sections.title: Section 7. Separability Clause

articles_and_sections.title: Section 8. Effectivity Clause

official_title: AN ORDINANCE AMENDING THE EXPLANATORY NOTE AND CERTAIN PROVISIONS OF ORDINANCE NO. 250 CREATING THE CITY MINING REGULATORY BOARD AND PROVIDING ANNUAL APPROPRIATION THEREFOR

articles_and_sections.title: Section 1 - Title
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section names the law as the ordinance that creates the City Small-Scale Mining Regulatory Board.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 2 - Definition of Terms

articles_and_sections.title: Section 3 - Powers and Functions

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section sets limits on how much land the Board can approve for mining permits.

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section says the City Mayor leads the Board meetings and explains when they should meet.

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section lists the costs for different mining permits and services.

eli5_summary: This law updates the rules for small-scale mining in Zamboanga City. It defines how the City Mining Regulatory Board works, sets the fees for mining permits, and explains the punishments for anyone who breaks these mining rules.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE CREATING THE ZAMBOANGA CITY COOPERATIVE DEVELOPMENT COUNCIL AND PROVIDING ANNUAL APPROPRIATIONS THEREFOR

articles_and_sections.title: Section 1 - Title
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section names the law the Zamboanga City Cooperative Development Council Ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 2 - Creation
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section creates a special group called the Zamboanga City Cooperative Development Council to help local cooperatives grow and work together.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 3 - Functions and Powers
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section lists the jobs of the council, such as helping cooperatives, solving their problems, and making sure they follow the rules.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 4 - Composition
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section explains who is in the council, including the City Mayor, government agency representatives, and people from the cooperatives themselves.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 5 - Executive Officers
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section lists the leaders of the council, like the Chairperson and Secretary.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 6 - Executive Director
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section describes the role of the Executive Director who manages the council's daily work and reports.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 7 - Creation of Committees
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section sets up smaller teams within the council to focus on specific tasks like training, planning, money, and solving arguments.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 8 - Elections
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section says that the council members will vote for their own leaders.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 9 - Meetings
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section sets the schedule for when the council members must meet to discuss their work.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 10 - Quorum
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section states that at least half of the members plus one must be present for the council to make official decisions.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 11 - Appropriation
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section gives the council 600,000 pesos every year to pay for its operations.

eli5_summary: This law creates a special council in Zamboanga City to help local cooperatives (groups of people working together for business) succeed. The council is made up of city leaders and cooperative members who work together to provide training, solve problems, and manage funds to help these groups grow.

amended_by_details.changes: Amended Section 4 to update the composition of the Zamboanga City Cooperative Development Council in accordance with CDA Memorandum Circular No. 2013-01.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE PROVIDING FOR THE CASH INCENTIVES OF REGISTERED SENIOR CITIZENS IN THE CITY OF ZAMBOANGA, SUBJECT TO APPLICABLE LAWS AND AUDITING RULES AND PROCEDURES
co_authors: HON. JUAN CLIMACO P. ELAGO II

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 1
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets the rule that registered senior citizens will receive a yearly cash gift during their birth month.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 2
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Determines the specific cash amount a senior citizen receives based on their age bracket, ranging from 60 years old up to 99 years old.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 3
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Instructs city offices and senior citizen organizations to create the rules for how this money will be distributed within 30 days.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 4
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Explains that the city government's regular budget will pay for these cash incentives.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 5
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires copies of this ordinance to be sent to the proper city departments for implementation.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 6
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Cancels any older city rules that go against this new ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 7
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States that if one part of this law is found invalid, the rest of the law still stays in place.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 8
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Says this law starts working as soon as the mayor approves it.

eli5_summary: Registered senior citizens in Zamboanga City will now receive a cash gift every year during their birth month. The older you get, the higher the cash amount you receive, ranging from 500 pesos to 2,000 pesos depending on your age group.
governing_agency: City Social Welfare and Development Office (CSWDO)

amendment_details.changes: Section 1 was amended to change the date of the Zamboanga City town fiesta (Fiesta Pilar) from December 8th to October 12th.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE REGULATING THE HOLDING OF FERIAS IN CELEBRATION OF BARANGAY FIESTAS, PROHIBITING GAMES OF CHANCE OR SHOWS IN FERIAS WHICH ARE CONTRARY TO LAWS, PUBLIC POLICY AND/OR PUBLIC MORALS, PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF AND FOR OTHER RELATED PURPOSES

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 1. TITLE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Names the law as the 'Barangay Feria Regulation Ordinance of the City of Zamboanga'.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 2. DEFINITION OF TERMS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Defines what betting, ferias (fairs or carnivals), and illegal games are.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 3. BARANGAY FERIA OPERATIONS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets the rules for holding a fair, such as getting a mayor's permit, following specific operating hours, staying away from schools and churches, keeping the area clean, and managing parking.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 4. PROHIBITED ACTS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Lists what fair operators cannot do, like running without a permit, breaking rules, offering illegal gambling, or letting young children enter without parents.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 5. ROLE OF THE BARANGAYS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires local barangay officials to help the city and police enforce these rules.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 6. ADMINISTRATIVE FINES
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Gives punishments for breaking the rules, including a 5,000 peso fine, losing business permits, and being banned from running fairs for two years.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 7. PENAL CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States that illegal gambling will be punished under existing national laws.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 8. SEPARABILITY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Ensures that if one part of this law is found invalid, the rest of the law stays in effect.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 9. REPEALING CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Cancels any older rules that go against this new ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 10. EFFECTIVITY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Says when the ordinance officially starts following the Local Government Code.

fines.penalty: Five Thousand Pesos (Php5,000.00) fine, revocation of business permit, and a two-year ban for three-time offenders.
fines.offense_level: Violation under paragraphs 1, 2, and 3 of Section 4

eli5_summary: This ordinance regulates carnivals and fairs (ferias) during barangay fiestas in Zamboanga City. It makes sure fairs have proper permits, follow safety and cleanliness rules, stay away from schools and churches, and completely ban illegal gambling and underage entry without parents.
governing_agency: City Mayor's Office / Philippine National Police

articles_and_sections.title: Section 4 - Roles and Functions

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section lists specific streets and areas where parking is prohibited or restricted to keep traffic moving smoothly.

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section creates the Zamboanga City Traffic Operations Management (ZCTOM) committee to oversee traffic planning.

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section sets rules for using the city's bus terminals, including fees for parking and cargo.

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section sets aside 5 million pesos for the city to buy two tow trucks.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 8 - Penalty Clause
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: People who hurt these trees will have to pay a fine or go to jail.

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Gives a 100% discount on penalties and interest until December 15, 2018, and a 50% discount from then until June 30, 2019.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 7. REPEALING CLAUSE

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 8. EFFECTIVITY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States when this ordinance officially starts following the Local Government Code.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE INSTITUTIONALIZING THE PROGRAMS, SERVICES, PRIVILEGES, AND BENEFITS FOR SOLO PARENTS AND THEIR CHILDREN, PRESCRIBING PENALTIES VIOLATIVE TO THIS ORDINANCE, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREOF AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES PURSUANT TO REPUBLIC ACT 11861, KNOWN AS THE EXPANDED SOLO PARENTS WELFARE ACT

articles_and_sections.title: Article I - Title, Policy, and Definition of Terms
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets the name of the ordinance, states the city's goal to support families, and defines important words used throughout the document.

articles_and_sections.title: Article II - Adoption Clause
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Formally adopts national laws supporting solo parents so they can be fully practiced in Zamboanga City.

articles_and_sections.title: Article III - Categories of Solo Parents, Documentary Requirements, and Issuance of Solo Parent Identification Card (SPIC) and Booklet
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Explains who qualifies as a solo parent, what papers are needed to prove it, and how to get an official ID card.

articles_and_sections.title: Article IV - Solo Parents Section (SPS) and Solo Parent Help Desk
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Creates a dedicated office and local help desks to assist solo parents and manage their applications and concerns.

articles_and_sections.title: Article V - Welfare Services, Privileges, and Benefits for Solo Parents
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Lists all the special help solo parents receive, such as cash assistance, free health insurance, scholarship priorities, and housing perks.

articles_and_sections.title: Article VI - Limitation and Termination of the Benefits of a Solo Parent
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Explains when solo parent benefits stop, such as when circumstances change or if the ID is not renewed.

articles_and_sections.title: Article VII - Recording and Maintaining a Solo Parents Database
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires the city to keep an updated list of all registered solo parents.

articles_and_sections.title: Article VIII - Ciudad de Zamboanga Dia y Semana de los Solo Mayores
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Declares a special week and day every April to celebrate and honor solo parents in the city.

articles_and_sections.title: Article IX - Final Provisions
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Covers funding, penalties for lying to get benefits, and when the law officially starts.

fines.penalty: Criminal prosecution under the Revised Penal Code and automatic cancellation of the Solo Parent ID, services, benefits, and privileges.

eli5_summary: Zamboanga City is rolling out special support, benefits, and cash assistance for solo parents and their children. Solo parents can get an official ID card that gives them perks like health insurance coverage, education priorities, housing assistance, and quarterly cash help if they qualify. Anyone who lies to get these benefits will face criminal charges and lose their ID.
governing_agency: City Social Welfare and Development Office (CSWDO)

official_title: AN ORDINANCE ESTABLISHING THE ZAMBOANGA CITY CENTER FOR INTEGRATED FRESHWATER RESEARCH, PRODUCTION, TECHNOLOGY TRANSFER, TRAINING, AND ECO-TOURISM AT BOG LAKE COVERING BARANGAYS CALARIAN, MALAGUTAY, AND SAN ROQUE, AND FOR OTHER RELATED PURPOSES

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 1. SHORT TITLE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Names the ordinance as the Center for Integrated Freshwater Research, Production, Technology Transfer, Training, and Eco-Tourism Ordinance of the City of Zamboanga.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 2. DECLARATION OF POLICY
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States the city's goal to protect freshwater resources, promote science and technology, support local fisheries, and encourage eco-tourism.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 3. DEFINITION OF TERMS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Defines key terms used throughout the ordinance like Center, Freshwater, Production, Research, and Eco-Tourism.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 4. OBJECTIVES

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 9. THE TECHNICAL ADVISORY BOARD
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Creates an advisory board consisting of local officials and agency heads to give technical guidance and policy recommendations.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 10. APPROPRIATION CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Allocates around Thirty Million Pesos annually from the city budget to fund the Center.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 11. SEPARABILITY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Ensures that if one part of the law is found invalid, the rest remains in effect.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 12. REPEALING CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Cancels older rules that conflict with this new ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 13. EFFECTIVITY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States when the ordinance officially becomes active.

eli5_summary: Zamboanga City is creating a special center at Bog Lake (covering Calarian, Malagutay, and San Roque) to study freshwater, grow fish and plants, teach people new farming technologies, and run an eco-tourism park. official_title: CORONA VIRUS DISEASE – 2019 (COVID-19) EMERGENCY ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF ZAMBOANGA

articles_and_sections.title: Section 1 - Title
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Names this rule the COVID-19 Emergency Ordinance of Zamboanga City.

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States the city's goal to fight COVID-19, protect health, and help people in need.

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets the timeframe that these rules apply, which is during the health emergency or calamity.

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Lists all the rules people must follow, such as wearing masks, staying home during lockdowns, observing curfews, and banning alcohol sales.

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires local neighborhoods to set up response teams to monitor and manage sick or suspected people.

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Promises extra financial and food help for poor and low-income families.

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires the city to create a plan to help the local economy recover after the pandemic.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 9 - Budgetary and Funding Requirement
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Allows the city to move money around in its budget to pay for emergency health and safety needs.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 10 - Penalty Clause
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Explains the fines and jail time for breaking the emergency rules.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 11 - Administrative Fines
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Gives people an option to pay a cash fine instead of going to court for certain rule violations.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 12 - Construction or Interpretation
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Ensures this local law does not conflict with national laws, which always take priority.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 13 - Separability Clause
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Says that if one part of this law is found illegal by a court, the rest of the rules still apply.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 14 - Repealing Clause
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Cancels any older local rules that clash with this new emergency ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 15 - Effectivity Clause
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Says this law starts right away after being published online or in the newspaper.

eli5_summary: During the COVID-19 pandemic, Zamboanga City put strict safety rules in place to keep everyone healthy. People had to wear masks, stay home during lockdowns, follow curfews, and avoid large gatherings. Anyone who broke these rules faced fines or jail time.
governing_agency: Zamboanga City Inter-Agency Task Force on COVID-19 / City Mayor's Office

official_title: AN ORDINANCE OPERATIONALIZING THE FREEDOM OF INFORMATION (FOI) IN THE CITY OF ZAMBOANGA, ESTABLISHING THE COMMUNITY BULLETIN INFORMATION PLATFORM, AND PROVIDING GUIDELINES AND APPROPRIATION THEREOF
authors: HON. JUAN CLIMACO P. ELAGO II

articles_and_sections.title: Section 1 - Title
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Names the ordinance as the 2021 FOI Ordinance of the City of Zamboanga.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 2 - Coverage
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Applies the rules to all government offices under the Zamboanga City Government.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 3 - Definition of Terms
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Defines what information, official records, public records, and bulletin platforms mean.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 4 - Access to Information
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Grants everyone the right to access public documents and official records unless they are restricted by law.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 5 - Mandatory Disclosure of Official and Public Records
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Lists specific government financial and operational reports that must be made publicly available.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 6 - Establishment of the FOI Transparency Bulletin Board
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets up physical bulletin boards in City Hall, the council building, public markets, and various barangays to display public records.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 7 - FOI Bulletin Information Platform
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires the city to create an online platform for public and official records.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 8 - Procedure in Accessing of Information
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Explains how citizens can file a written request for documents and how long the office has to reply.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 9 - Exceptions
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Lists sensitive topics like national security, personal privacy, and ongoing investigations that cannot be shared.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 10 - Application and Interpretation
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Establishes that government offices should always lean toward releasing information unless it clearly breaks the rules.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 11 - Keeping of Records
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires government offices to properly organize and store their important documents for easy public retrieval.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 12 - Administrative Liability
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States that public employees who fail to follow this ordinance can face administrative punishment.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 13 - Penalties
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Outlines penalties for erring employees, ranging from a reprimand to suspension, and potentially dismissal for repeat offenses.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 14 - Appropriation Clause
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets aside an initial budget of 500,000 pesos to fund the FOI program.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 15 - Separability Clause
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Ensures the rest of the ordinance stays valid even if a court strikes down one part.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 16 - Repealing Clause
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Cancels any older rules that conflict with this new ordinance.

fines.penalty: Reprimand
Suspension of one (1) to thirty (30) days
May serve as a ground for dismissal from the service in accordance with Civil Service Commission rules

eli5_summary: This ordinance gives citizens the right to look at city government records, budgets, and transactions. It sets up physical bulletin boards and an online platform where people can easily see how the city is spending public money. If city officials refuse to share public information without a valid legal reason, they can face suspension or job loss.
governing_agency: Office of the City Mayor / Sangguniang Panlungsod

official_title: AN ORDINANCE IMPOSING A CITY-WIDE CURFEW FOR CHILDREN FROM 10:00 O’CLOCK IN THE EVENING TO 4:00 O’CLOCK IN THE MORNING OF THE FOLLOWING DAY, HEREBY ESTABLISHING THE APPROPRIATE PROCEDURE FOR THEIR CUSTODY AND SAFEKEEPING

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 1. TITLE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Names the ordinance as the 'ORDINANCE IMPOSING CURFEW FOR CHILDREN IN ZAMBOANGA CITY.'

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 2. COVERAGE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Applies to all children within Zamboanga City.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 3. DEFINITION OF TERMS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Defines what a child is (under 18 or unable to care for themselves), curfew hours, and emergencies.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 4. CURFEW HOURS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets the curfew time from 10:00 PM to 4:00 AM the next day for children roaming or hanging out outside.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 5. PROHIBITIONS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Bans children from being out during curfew without a good reason, and prohibits parents from allowing it.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 6. EXEMPTIONS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Lists valid reasons to be out during curfew, such as being with parents, attending night classes, emergencies, or authorized work.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 7. PROCEDURE AGAINST "CHILDREN AT RISK"
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Explains how children found out during curfew are brought home or to barangay officials safely without being treated like criminals.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 8. INTERVENTIONS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Details counseling and community service steps for children who break the curfew multiple times.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 9. Penalty for the Parent or Guardian
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets fines and community service penalties for parents who let their kids break the curfew.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 10. SEPARABILITY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States that if one part of the law is found invalid, the rest remains active.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 11. REPEALING CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Cancels older local rules that conflict with this curfew ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 12. EFFECTIVITY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States the ordinance takes effect after being published in a newspaper.

fines.penalty: Reprimand and fine of Php500.00, or community service for two (2) hours.
Fine of Php1,000.00, or community service for three (3) hours.
Fine of Php2,000.00, or community service for five (5) hours.
Php5,000.00 and community service for ten (10) hours.

eli5_summary: Minors under 18 years old are not allowed to roam or hang out outside their homes from 10:00 PM to 4:00 AM unless they have a valid reason like school, work, or emergencies. If caught, they will be safely brought home or to the barangay hall, but their parents can face fines or community service if they let it happen.
governing_agency: City Social Welfare and Development Office / Barangay Governments / Philippine National Police

articles_and_sections.title: Section 1 - Title

articles_and_sections.title: Section 2 - Purpose and General Coverage
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Explains that this rule helps law enforcement pay for COVID-19 tests and keeps everyone safe during the pandemic.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 3 - Declaration of Policy

articles_and_sections.title: Section 5 - Procedure

articles_and_sections.title: Section 6 - Appropriation
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets aside city government funds to pay for the required testing expenses.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 7 - Separability Clause
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Ensures that if one part of the law is found invalid, the rest of the law still applies.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 8 - Repealing Clause
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Cancels any older rules that conflict with this new ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 9 - Effectivity
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States that the law becomes active after it is published in a local newspaper.

eli5_summary: This ordinance requires prisoners and detainees in Zamboanga City to get tested for COVID-19 using an RT-PCR swab test before they are released, transferred, or brought into jail facilities. official_title: AN ORDINANCE INSTITUTING POLICIES FOR THE PROTECTION AND WELFARE OF DOMESTIC WORKERS (KASAMBAHAY) WITHIN THE TERRITORIAL JURISDICTION OF THE CITY OF ZAMBOANGA

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 1. TITLE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Names the ordinance as the Domestic Workers (Kasambahay) Ordinance of the City of Zamboanga.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 2. PURPOSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States the goal to protect household helpers from abuse while also protecting employer rights.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 3. COVERAGE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Explains who is covered by the law, such as yayas, cooks, and gardeners, and who is excluded.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 4. DEFINITION OF TERMS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Defines important words used in the ordinance like debt bondage, domestic worker, and agency.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 5. MODE OF HIRING
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Allows hiring either directly or through a licensed employment agency.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 6. COST OF HIRING
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires the employer to pay for the hiring costs.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 7. DEPLOYMENT EXPENSES
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Makes the employer pay for travel expenses to bring the worker from their hometown.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 8. PRE-EMPLOYMENT REQUIREMENTS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Lists documents like medical and police clearances that can be required before hiring.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 9. EMPLOYMENT CONTRACT
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Mandates a written contract in a language both parties understand before work begins.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 10. RIGHTS AND PRIVILEGES OF THE KASAMBAHAY
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Outlines minimum wage, benefits, rest periods, and other rights for domestic workers.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 11. MODE OF PAYMENT OF WAGES
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires wages to be paid in cash, not items or promissory notes.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 12. FREQUENCY OF PAYMENT OF WAGES
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Mandates that wages must be paid at least once a month.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 13. SERVICE INCENTIVE LEAVE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Grants at least 5 days of paid yearly leave to workers who have served for one year.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 14. THIRTEENTH-MONTH PAY
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Ensures a 13th-month pay given by December 24 every year for workers with at least one month of service.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 15. SOCIAL SECURITY BENEFITS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Mandates coverage by SSS, PhilHealth, and Pag-IBIG, with contributions paid by the employer.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 16. RIGHTS AND PRIVILEGES OF THE EMPLOYER
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Lists the rights of employers, such as requiring documents and demanding replacements.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 17. PAY SLIP
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires employers to give pay slips showing earnings and deductions and keep copies for 3 years.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 18. REGISTRATION AND ENROLMENT TO SSS, PHILHEALTH AND PAG-IBIG
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires employers to register as employers and enroll their domestic workers into the government benefit systems.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 19. PRE-TERMINATION OF EMPLOYMENT
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Allows ending the contract early by mutual agreement or with a 5-day notice.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 20. TERMINATION OF EMPLOYMENT INITIATED BY THE KASAMBAHAY
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Lists valid reasons for a domestic worker to quit early, such as abuse or contract violations.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 21. TERMINATION OF EMPLOYMENT INITIATED BY THE EMPLOYER
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Lists valid reasons for an employer to dismiss a domestic worker early, such as dishonesty or poor performance.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 22. BARANGAY KASAMBAHAY DESK (BKD)
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Establishes a desk in every barangay to register domestic workers and handle initial complaints.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 23. CREATION OF THE KASAMBAHAY ADJUDICATION BOARD (KAB) AND ITS COMPOSITION
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Creates a board to hear and decide cases that cannot be resolved at the barangay level.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 24. DUTIES, POWERS AND FUNCTIONS OF THE KASAMBAHAY ADJUDICATION BOARD (KAB)
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Details the KAB's power to receive complaints, hold hearings, and impose penalties.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 25. UNLAWFUL ACTS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Bans illegal practices like employing children under 15, withholding wages, and debt bondage.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 26. ADMINISTRATIVE PENALTIES
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets fines for breaking the rules, starting at 3,000 pesos for a first offense.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 27. DIA DE KASAMBAHAY
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Declares January 18 of every year as Kasambahay Day in Zamboanga City.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 28. REPEALING CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Cancels any older city rules that conflict with this ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 29. SEPARABILITY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States that if one part of the law is found invalid, the rest remains in effect.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 30. EFFECTIVITY
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets when the ordinance officially becomes active.

fines.offense_level: 3rd and succeeding offenses and for violation committed against working children

eli5_summary: This ordinance protects domestic workers (kasambahay) in Zamboanga City by guaranteeing them fair wages, benefits like SSS and PhilHealth, and rest periods. It requires employers to register their workers at the barangay, provide written contracts, and avoid abusive practices. Fines and a special board are set up to punish employers who break these rules.
governing_agency: Barangay Kasambahay Desk / Kasambahay Adjudication Board

articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires the school to have standard buildings, multi-purpose facilities, and follow accessibility and green building laws.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 5 - Teaching Staff and Other Allied Support
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States that the city government will initially fund teachers and staff until the national government takes over.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 6 - Repealing Clause
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Cancels any previous rules that go against this new ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 7 - Separability Clause

articles_and_sections.title: Section 8 - Effectivity Clause
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Says when the law officially starts following local government rules.

eli5_summary: The city government is creating a new integrated school in Barangay Kasanyangan. The city will provide funds to buy land, build eco-friendly facilities, and pay for teachers until the national government takes over.
