official_title: AN ORDINANCE RECLASSIFYING A PRODUCTION AGRICULTURAL SUB-ZONE KNOWN AS LOT NO. 297, CONTAINING AN AREA OF 48,025 SQUARE ES, SITUATED AT BARANGAY BUENAVISTA, THIS CITY, TO RESIDENTIAL ZONE-1

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 1
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Reclassifies a specific piece of land (Lot No. 297 in Barangay Buenavista) from agricultural use to residential use.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 2
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires that the land must be used following the city's zoning rules and laws.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 3
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Ensures that if one part of this law is found invalid, the rest of the law still applies.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 4
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Cancels any older local rules that go against this new law.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 5
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States that this law becomes active right after it is approved.

eli5_summary: The city government changed the official use of a large piece of farm land in Barangay Buenavista so that houses and residential buildings can be built on it instead.
governing_agency: City Zoning Board of Adjustments and Appeals

official_title: AN ORDINANCE RECLASSIFYING AN AGRICULTURAL LAND KNOWN AS LOT 2-A-1, PSD-09-044369, COVERED BY TCT NO. T-159,905, AND CONTAINING AN AREA OF 2,800 SQUARE METERS, SITUATED AT BARANGAY SAN ROQUE, THIS CITY, FROM IRRIGATED RICE LAND TO A RESIDENTIAL LAND

articles_and_sections.title: Section 1
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section officially changes the land use classification of a specific 2,800 square meter lot in Barangay San Roque from agricultural to residential.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 2
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section states that the new rule starts working as soon as it is approved.

eli5_summary: This law changes a piece of land in Barangay San Roque from being used for farming to being used for building houses. This was done because the land is no longer good for growing rice and is surrounded by houses.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE GRANTING MR. CESAR J. BAHIDJAN A FRANCHISE TO OPERATE AND MAINTAIN A FLEA MARKET OR “TALIPAPA” AT BARANGAY SAN ROQUE, THIS CITY

articles_and_sections.title: Section 1 - Grant of Franchise and Conditions
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Grants Mr. Cesar J. Bahidjan a 5-year permit to run a local market in Barangay San Roque provided he follows rules regarding taxes, traffic, cleanliness, and building permits.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 2 - Withdrawal or Suspension
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Allows the city government to cancel or suspend the market permit if the owner breaks any of the terms or city rules.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 3 - Renewal Application
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires the owner to submit an application to renew the permit at least two months before it expires.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 4 - Repealing Clause
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Cancels Ordinance No. 368, Series of 2011.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 5 - Effectivity
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States that the law takes effect according to the rules of the Local Government Code.

eli5_summary: This ordinance gives Mr. Cesar J. Bahidjan official permission to run a local flea market or 'talipapa' in Barangay San Roque for five years. The market owner must follow strict city rules about cleanliness, permits, safety, and paying local taxes. If the market breaks these rules, the city can take away the permit.

amendment_details.changes: Completely repealed and replaced by the new franchise ordinance.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE FURTHER AMENDING SECTION 4 OF ORDINANCE NO. 540, AS AMENDED BY ORDINANCE NO. 577, AND FOR OTHER RELATED PURPOSES

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 1. AMENDATORY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Extends the deadline for paying off housing balances without extra fines and penalties until May 31, 2025.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 2. REPEALING CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Cancels any older rules that clash with this new deadline extension.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 3. SEPARABILITY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States that if one part of this rule is found illegal, the rest of the rule still stays valid.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 4. EFFECTIVITY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Says this new rule starts right after it is published in a local newspaper.

eli5_summary: If you live in a city housing project, you get more time (until May 31, 2025) to pay off what you owe without extra penalties piling up. This helps families catch up on their payments easier.
governing_agency: City Housing and Land Management Office

amendment_details.changes: Repealed in its entirety, removing the renaming of Veterans Avenue to Assemblyman Joaquin F. Enriquez, Jr. Avenue.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE CREATING THE NEW PEOPLE’S LAW ENFORCEMENT BOARD (PLEB) OF THE CITY OF ZAMBOANGA, AND FOR OTHER RELATED PURPOSES
co_authors: Hon. Juan Climaco P. Elago II

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 1. CREATION
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Creates the People's Law Enforcement Board (PLEB) in Zamboanga City to handle complaints against police officers.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 2. FUNCTIONS, POWERS, AND DUTIES
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Gives the PLEB the power to listen to and decide on complaints made by citizens against police officers.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 3. COMPOSITION
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Explains who makes up the board, including a council member, a barangay captain, and community members.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 4. TERM OF OFFICE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets the term limit for board members to three years.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 5. QUORUM
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets the rules for how many board members need to be present to hold a meeting and make a decision.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 6. PROCEDURE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Defines the official rules and guidelines the board must follow when handling cases.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 7. DISQUALIFICATION BY REASON OF AFFINITY AND CONSANGUINITY
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Prevents board members from handling cases involving their relatives to keep things fair.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 8. APPROPRIATION
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Ensures that the city budget provides funds for the operation and maintenance of the PLEB.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 9. SEPARABILITY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States that if one part of this law is found illegal, the rest of the law stays in effect.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 10. REPEALING CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Cancels any older rules that conflict with this new ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 11. EFFECTIVITY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States when this ordinance officially starts being the law.

eli5_summary: This ordinance creates a special board called the People's Law Enforcement Board (PLEB) in Zamboanga City. Citizens can go to this board if they have complaints or problems with local police officers. The board is made up of community and local government representatives who investigate and decide on these complaints.

amendment_details.changes: Section 1 was amended to change the date of the Zamboanga City town fiesta (Fiesta Pilar) from December 8th to October 12th.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE GRANTING GARCELO INC. A FRANCHISE TO OPERATE AND MAINTAIN A PRIVATE POULTRY DRESSING PLANT AT BARANGAY TULUNGATUNG, ZAMBOANGA CITY, IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE PROVISIONS OF SECTION 12, OF ORDINANCE NO. 2017-178, AS AMENDED BY ORDINANCE NO. 2017-179, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE MEAT INSPECTION CODE OF ZAMBOANGA CITY

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 1
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Grants a 5-year franchise to Garcelo Inc. to operate a poultry dressing plant in Barangay Tulungatung under specific health, sanitation, and operational conditions, requiring a total franchise fee of 100,000 Pesos payable in installments.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 2
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States that the government can cancel the franchise if the company breaks any rules or laws.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 3
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires the company to apply for franchise renewal at least six months before it expires.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 4
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Ensures that if the city's Meat Inspection Code changes in the future, those new rules will automatically apply to this franchise.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 5
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Declares that if any part of this ordinance is found illegal, the rest of it remains valid and active.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 6
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States that this law becomes effective right after it is published in a newspaper.

eli5_summary: The city government gave Garcelo Inc. permission to run a chicken cleaning and processing plant in Barangay Tulungatung for five years. The company must pay a fee and follow strict cleanliness, health, and traffic rules.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE DECLARING AND OBSERVING NOVEMBER 14 OF EVERY YEAR AS “DIA DE CESAR” AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS FOR THE NECESSARY EXPENSES THEREOF

articles_and_sections.title: Section 1
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Declares November 14 of every year as 'Dia de Cesar' to honor the memory and contributions of Mayor Cesar C. Climaco.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 2 - Implementing Body
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: The Cultural and Historical Committee is responsible for planning and organizing the celebration.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 3 - Funding
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets aside 50,000 pesos from the city budget every year to pay for the celebration.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 4 - Effectivity
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States when the law officially starts working.

eli5_summary: This law makes November 14 a special day in Zamboanga City to remember and honor former Mayor Cesar C. Climaco. The city will set aside money every year to help pay for events and activities to celebrate his life.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE INSTITUTIONALIZING AND GRANTING MASTERS AND/OR DOCTORAL DEGREE SCHOLARSHIP PROGRAM TO DESERVING AND QUALIFIED OFFICIALS AND EMPLOYEES OF THE CITY OF ZAMBOANGA, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER RELATED PURPOSES
co_authors: HON. JUAN CLIMACO P. ELAGO II

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 1. TITLE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Names the ordinance as the 'City of Zamboanga’s Scholarship Program for its Officers and Employees Ordinance'.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 2. COVERAGE, ELIGIBILITY AND LIMITATION
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets the rules on who can apply, stating it is for permanent city employees wanting to take full-time graduate degrees aligned with city needs.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 3. SELECTION CRITERIA
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Lists the requirements to qualify, such as working for 5 years, getting good performance ratings, and being under 56 years old.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 4. AREAS OF SPECIALIZATION
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Lists the approved fields of study like agriculture, engineering, public health, law, and public management.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 5. SCHOLARSHIP PRIVILEGES
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Details what financial help scholars get, including tuition aid, book allowances, and continuing to receive their salary while studying.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 6. TERMINATION OF SCHOLARSHIP
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Explains that the city can cancel the scholarship and demand a refund if the employee fails their subjects or quits.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 7. SERVICE OBLIGATION
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires scholars to work back for the city for a specific number of years after finishing their studies.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 8. PAYBACK OBLIGATION
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Gives the formula for how much money an employee must pay back if they resign or fail to complete their service obligation.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 9. RESPONSIBILITIES OF THE SCHOLAR
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Lists the duties of the scholar, like signing a contract, keeping good grades, and submitting a thesis.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 10. GUIDELINES AND OTHER ISSUANCES
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Allows the Personnel Development Committee to create more detailed rules with the Mayor's approval.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 11. APPROPRIATION CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets aside an initial budget of 5 million pesos to fund the scholarship program.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 12. REPEALING CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Cancels any past rules that conflict with this new scholarship ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 13. SEPARABILITY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States that if one part of this law is found illegal, the rest of the law stays in effect.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 14. EFFECTIVITY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Says the ordinance starts in School Year 2022 after it is published in a newspaper.

eli5_summary: The city government created a scholarship program to help permanent city employees pay for their Master's, Doctoral, or Law degrees. In exchange for getting their tuition paid and keeping their salary while studying, these employees must work for the city for a few extra years.
governing_agency: Personnel Development Committee (PDC) / City Human Resource Management Office

amendment_details.changes: Amended Paragraph (c) of Section 6, Article IV regarding the routing of cargo trucks. It restricts trucks over 5 gross tons on Guardia National Street, Governor Lim Avenue, Tomas Claudio Street, and parts of Mayor N. Valderosa Street from 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM, and bans all cargo trucks on Normal Road from 6:00 AM to 6:00 PM on school days. The rest of the original Traffic Code remains functional.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE CREATING THE INVESTMENT PROMOTIONS OFFICE IN THE CITY OF ZAMBOANGA, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

articles_and_sections.title: Section 1 - Title
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section names the law as the Investment Promotions Office ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 2 - Creation
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section officially creates a new office in the city government called the Investment Promotions Office.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 3 - Purposes
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section lists the goals of the new office, such as helping businesses, sharing information, and making it easier for companies to invest in Zamboanga.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 4 - Composition
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section explains that the office will be led by an officer chosen by the Mayor and staffed by existing city employees.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 5 - Qualifications
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section sets the rules for who can be the Investment Promotions Officer, requiring them to be a local resident with a college degree and relevant work experience.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 6 - Repealing Clause
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section cancels any older rules that conflict with this new law.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 7 - Separability Clause
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section ensures that if one part of this law is found to be illegal, the rest of the law still stays in effect.

eli5_summary: The city created a special office to help attract more businesses and investments to Zamboanga. This office is responsible for making it easier for companies to set up shop here, which helps create more jobs for everyone.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE IMPLEMENTING FORCED EVACUATION AS A RESORT WHEN A DISASTER OR EMERGENCY HAS BEEN DECLARED IN THE CITY OF ZAMBOANGA AND DANGER OF LOSS OF LIVES BECOMES IMMINENT, PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
authors: Hon. Juan Climaco P. Elago II

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 1. Declaration of Policy
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Declares that the city's priority is to protect residents and lessen the damage caused by disasters.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 2. DEFINITION OF TERMS As used in this Ordinance
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Defines important words like disaster, imminent danger, evacuation, and forced evacuation.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 3. TRAINING AND ORIENTATION ON DISASTER RISK REDUCTION AND MANAGEMENT
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires local disaster offices to train residents and spread awareness on safety rules before bad weather seasons.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 4. PROHIBITION OF FISHING VESSELS AND FISHING ACTIVITIES
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Bans small boats and fishing vessels from going to sea when storm signals are raised.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 5. FORCED EVACUATION
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Explains how the Mayor can order forced evacuations to safe centers when severe danger threatens lives.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 6. ENLISTMENT OF ASSISTANCE OF OTHER GOVERNMENT AGENCIES
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Allows the city to ask police, military, firefighters, and coast guard to help conduct evacuations.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 7. REFUSAL OF LOCAL RESIDENTS TO ABIDE BY THE DECLARATION OF FORCED EVACUATION OR AFTER EVACUATING, GO BACK TO THEIR RESPECTIVE HOMES WITHOUT AN ORDER ALLOWING THEM TO DO SO
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Gives officers authority to safely move residents who refuse to leave dangerous areas or try to return too soon.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 8. PENALTY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets punishment for anyone who refuses orders or violates rules during a forced evacuation.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 9. REPEALING CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Cancels any old local rules that conflict with this evacuation law.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 10. EFFECTIVITY
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States that this ordinance takes effect immediately.

fines.penalty: Fine not exceeding Php5,000.00 or imprisonment not exceeding 1 year

eli5_summary: This law allows the city mayor to force people to evacuate their homes when dangerous disasters threaten lives. It prohibits fishermen and boats from sailing during storm warnings and allows authorities to safely relocate people who refuse to leave. Violators who disobey evacuation orders can be fined or jailed.
governing_agency: City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (CDRRMO)

official_title: AN ORDINANCE ADOPTING THE ZONING REGULATIONS OF THE CITY OF ZAMBOANGA AND PROVIDING FOR THE ADMINISTRATION, ENFORCEMENT, AND AMENDMENT THEREOF AND FOR THE REPEAL OF ALL ORDINANCES IN CONFLICT THEREWITH
authors: HON. JUAN CLIMACO P. ELAGO II

articles_and_sections.title: Article I - Title of the Ordinance
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States the official name of the ordinance, which is the Zoning Ordinance of 2018 of the City of Zamboanga.

articles_and_sections.title: Article II - Authority and Purpose
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Explains the legal basis and the main goals of the ordinance, such as guiding city growth, protecting the environment, and ensuring public safety.

articles_and_sections.title: Article III - Definition of Terms
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Defines special words and technical terms used throughout the ordinance so everyone understands what they mean.

articles_and_sections.title: Article IV - Zone Classifications
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Divides the city into different areas or zones, such as residential, commercial, agricultural, and industrial zones.

articles_and_sections.title: Article V - Zone Policies and Regulations
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Details the specific rules, building limits, and activities allowed in each base zone and overlay zone.

articles_and_sections.title: Article VI - General Regulations
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets standard rules for building heights, lot occupancy, open spaces, and easements that apply across the city.

articles_and_sections.title: Article VII - General District Regulations
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Provides guidelines on setbacks, parking spaces, traffic generators, and pollution control for districts.

articles_and_sections.title: Article VIII - Supplementary Regulations
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Covers special permits, innovative designs, fees, and charges for development projects.

articles_and_sections.title: Article IX - Performance Standards
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets environmental and site development rules to protect nature and local resources.

articles_and_sections.title: Article X - Mitigating Devices
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Explains how property owners can request special relief or exceptions from certain zoning rules due to unique hardships.

articles_and_sections.title: Article XI - Administration and Enforcement
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Outlines the rules for getting clearances, permits, handling appeals, and enforcing penalties for violations.

eli5_summary: This ordinance sets up a master plan for Zamboanga City, deciding which areas can be used for building homes, opening businesses, farming, or protecting nature. It helps the city grow safely and orderly while protecting the environment and public health.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE AMENDING SECTION 4 OF CITY ORDINANCE NO. 254 OTHERWISE KNOWN AS “AN ORDINANCE CREATING THE ZAMBOANGA CITY COOPERATIVE DEVELOPMENT COUNCIL AND PROVIDING ANNUAL APPROPRIATIONS THEREFOR”
authors: Hon. Atty. Juan Climaco P. Elago II

articles_and_sections.title: Section 1 - Composition
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Updates Section 4 of City Ordinance No. 254 to specify who sits on the Zamboanga City Cooperative Development Council, including local officials and national government representatives.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 2 - Repealing Clause
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Cancels or modifies any existing local laws that conflict with this ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 3 - Separability Clause
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States that if any portion of this law is declared invalid, the remaining sections will stay in effect.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 4 - Effectivity
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Specifies that this ordinance takes effect 15 days after its approval.

eli5_summary: This ordinance updates the membership list for the Zamboanga City Cooperative Development Council. It adds specific local officials and national government agency members to follow national cooperative guidelines.

amendment_details.changes: Amended Section 4 to update the composition of the Zamboanga City Cooperative Development Council in accordance with CDA Memorandum Circular No. 2013-01.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE ESTABLISHING A HIGH SCHOOL IN THE BARANGAY OF TALUKSANGAY, ZAMBOANGA CITY, AND PROVIDING AN INITIAL APPROPRIATION THEREOF

articles_and_sections.title: Section 1 - Title
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section names the ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 2 - Site
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section identifies the location for the new high school in Barangay Taluksangay.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 3 - Initial Appropriation
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This sets aside 2.1 million pesos to build a two-story, six-room school building.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 4 - Source of Initial Appropriation
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This tells the city budget officer where to get the money for the school construction.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 5 - Maintenance and Other Operating Expenses
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This provides an extra 50,000 pesos from the city for school maintenance.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 6 - Teaching Staff, Administrative Personnel and Other Allied Support
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This explains that the Department of Education will handle the hiring and assignment of teachers and staff.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 7 - Procedure for Processing
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This outlines the steps the Mayor and school officials must take to get the school officially approved and running.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 8 - Commencement of Classes
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This explains when classes will officially start based on government approval.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 9 - Temporary Holding of Classes
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This allows students to use the local elementary school building while the new high school is being built.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 10 - Effectivity
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This states that the law starts working as soon as it is approved.

eli5_summary: This ordinance creates a new public high school in Barangay Taluksangay to make it easier for children in that area to go to school. The city is providing money to build the school building and help with its maintenance.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE GRANTING ALIXANDRA RECREATION CENTER CORPORATION A FRANCHISE TO OPERATE AND MAINTAIN A COCKPIT AT PRESA MAYOR, TUMAGA, ZAMBOANGA CITY

articles_and_sections.title: Section 1
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Grants a 5-year franchise to Alixandra Recreation Center Corporation to run a cockpit, subject to specific rules on location, fees, and facility standards.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 2
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Authorizes the City Mayor to issue a permit for the cockpit's operation once all requirements are met.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 3
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Requires that any special derby events must be held at this specific location and benefit approved organizations.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 4
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Allows the city to cancel or suspend the franchise if the owner breaks any rules or laws.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 5
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States when the ordinance officially begins to take effect.

fines.penalty: Withdrawal or suspension of the franchise

eli5_summary: The city is giving a company permission to run a cockpit in Tumaga for five years. They must follow strict rules about safety, cleanliness, and paying fees to the city, or they could lose their permit.

amended_by_details.changes: The entire ordinance is repealed by Section 5.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE AMENDING SECTION 3 (A), (1) AND SECTION 4 (3) OF ORDINANCE NO. 332, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS “THE ZAMBOANGA CITY SCHOLARSHIP ORDINANCE”, AS AMENDED BY ORDINANCE NO. 370, AND FOR OTHER RELATED PURPOSES
authors: HON. JUAN CLIMACO P. ELAGO II

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 1
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Updates the city scholarship program to give qualified top high school graduates 5,000 pesos per semester for school fees, books, or living needs since tuition is already free.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 2
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Clarifies that scholarship applicants or their siblings cannot receive multiple government or private scholarships at the same time, except for free tuition under national law.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 3
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Makes the new scholarship changes start applying from the 2018-2019 school year.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 4
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States that if any part of this rule is found illegal, the rest of the rule still applies.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 5
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Changes older city rules that conflict with this new scholarship update.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 6
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets the date when this new scholarship rule officially becomes active.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE CREATING THE TRAFFIC AND TRANSPORT ENGINEERING, PLANNING, MANAGEMENT, AND ENFORCEMENT DIVISION UNDER THE OFFICE OF THE CITY MAYOR, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER RELATED PURPOSES

articles_and_sections.title: Section 2 - Organizational Structure

articles_and_sections.title: Section 3 - General Functions, Duties and Responsibilities of the Division
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Outlines the main duties of the new division, which include enforcing traffic rules, planning road safety, managing the impounding area, and using modern tech for traffic monitoring.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 5 - Functions, Duties and Responsibilities of the Traffic and Transport Management and Enforcement Section

articles_and_sections.title: Section 6 - Transitory Provision

articles_and_sections.title: Section 9 - Repealing Clause

articles_and_sections.title: Section 10 - Effectivity Clause

This team will handle everything from street officers and impounding areas to high-tech traffic cameras. It helps make sure traffic rules are properly enforced under the Office of the City Mayor.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE INSTITUTIONALIZING, PROMOTING AND DEVELOPING ORGANIC AGRICULTURE IN ZAMBOANGA CITY, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
co_authors: HON. JUAN CLIMACO P. ELAGO II

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 1. TITLE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States the official name of this ordinance as the Organic Agriculture Ordinance of Zamboanga City.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 2. DECLARATION OF POLICY
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Declares the city's commitment to protecting food security, health, safety, and nature through organic farming.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 3. DECLARATION OF PRINCIPLES
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Outlines the main rules of organic agriculture, focusing on biodiversity, supporting small farmers, and climate change action.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 4. DEFINITION OF TERMS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Defines key terms used throughout the ordinance such as biopesticides, buffer zones, and organic agriculture.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 5. ORGANIC AGRICULTURAL ZONES
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets aside specific areas protected from chemical pollution and GMOs to be used strictly for organic farming.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 6. ORGANIC CENTERS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Establishes an Organic Trading Post at Sta. Cruz Bagsakan Center to promote and sell organic goods.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 7. CONSERVATION OF INDIGENOUS FARM PRACTICES
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Protects traditional and indigenous farming and seed-saving methods.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 8. ORGANIC GENE/SEED BANK
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Creates a seed bank to collect, save, and supply local organic seeds.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 9. SUPPORT SERVICE TO ORGANIC FARMERS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Provides training, marketing, and fair trade support to local organic farmers.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 10. ACCESS TO CREDIT FOR SMALL AND ORGANIC FARMERS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Helps small organic farmers easily access financial services and credit programs.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 11. BIOLOGICAL AND BOTANICAL CONTROL
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Encourages natural methods instead of chemical pesticides to control pests.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 12. IMPLEMENTATION MECHANISMS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Gives the City Agriculturist's Office the job of carrying out and managing the organic program.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 13. ORGANIC AGRICULTURE MANAGEMENT COUNCIL
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Creates a special council led by the Mayor to guide and oversee the city's organic farming program.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 14. APPROPRIATION
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets aside a dedicated budget to fund the city's organic farming activities.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 15. INCENTIVES TO FARMERS, SCHOOLS AND BARANGAYS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Rewards and gives financial support to schools, barangays, and farmers who successfully practice organic farming.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 16. STANDARD-SETTING
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Creates local standards for organic products using biodegradable waste and national guidelines.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 17. CAPACITY-BUILDING
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Provides ongoing training and education about organic farming for schools and the public.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 18. RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Creates a research plan to continuously improve organic farming methods in partnership with national agencies.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 19. PROMOTION OF URBAN ORGANIC AGRICULTURE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Encourages organic farming in city areas using new technologies and food waste.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 20. IMPLEMENTING RULES AND REGULATIONS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Authorizes the Mayor to create detailed rules to properly enforce this ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 21. SEPARABILITY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Ensures that if one part of this law is found invalid, the rest of the law still applies.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 22. REPEALING CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Cancels any older city rules that conflict with this new ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 23. EFFECTIVITY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States that this ordinance becomes active right after approval.

eli5_summary: This law helps Zamboanga City grow more healthy, chemical-free food by supporting local organic farmers, setting up safe farming zones, creating trading posts, and providing training and money for organic agriculture.

amendment_details.changes: Modified provisions regarding motorized tricycle routes on Corcuera Street and near City Hall, and specified pedestrian movement enforcement.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 13 - Repealing Clause
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Cancels older rules that go against this new ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 14 - Separability Clause
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Ensures that if one part of this law is found illegal, the rest remains active.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 15 - Effectivity Clause
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States when this ordinance officially starts following the Local Government Code.

eli5_summary: Zamboanga City is giving registered daycare workers a monthly allowance of 5,000 pesos, free uniforms, PhilHealth coverage, free medical care, and loyalty bonuses. This law helps take care of the people who teach and look after young children in every barangay.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 1 - Title

articles_and_sections.title: Section 2 - General Policy
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: The city wants to help farmers by providing cold storage to keep their crops from spoiling.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 3 - Definition of Terms
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This section explains technical words used in the law, like what 'cold storage' or 'agricultural produce' means.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 4 - Specific Objectives
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: The goal is to stop food from rotting, help the city earn money, and provide a place to sort and pack vegetables.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 5 - Management of the Facility
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: The City Administrator's office is in charge of running the cold storage facility.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 6 - Organizational Structure

articles_and_sections.title: Section 7 - Duties and Responsibilities
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: This explains what the technicians and workers do, like fixing machines and keeping track of stored food.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 8 - Role and Responsibilities of City Administrator's Office
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: The City Administrator oversees the facility and makes sure it runs well.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 9 - Roles and Responsibilities of the City Treasurer's Office
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: The City Treasurer is responsible for collecting storage fees and giving receipts.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 10 - Roles and Responsibilities of City Agriculturist's Office
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: The City Agriculturist helps farmers use the facility and keeps track of data.

articles_and_sections.title: Section 11 - Storage Fees and Other Charges

articles_and_sections.title: Section 12 - Adjustments of Storage Fees and Charges

articles_and_sections.title: Section 13 - Budgetary Appropriation
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: The city will set aside money in its budget to pay for the facility's operations.

official_title: AN ORDINANCE PROHIBITING GOVERNMENT OFFICIALS/EMPLOYEES, PRIVATE INDIVIDUALS, GROUPS, AND BUSINESS ESTABLISHMENTS IN ACCEPTING PANTAWID PAMILYANG PILIPINO PROGRAM (4PS) CASH CARDS AND OTHER PROGRAM DOCUMENTS AS LOAN COLLATERAL OR SECURITY CREDIT

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 1. TITLE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Names the ordinance as the law prohibiting the use of 4Ps cash cards and documents as loan collateral.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 2. DECLARATION OF POLICY
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States that the city wants to protect 4Ps beneficiaries from predators who take their cash cards as security for loans.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 3. DEFINITION OF TERMS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Defines important words used in the ordinance like pawning, pawner, pawnee, and persuasion.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 4. SPECIAL INTER-AGENCY STRUCTURE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Creates special councils to handle complaints and enforce the rules regarding 4Ps cash card pawning.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 5. POWERS AND JURISDICTIONS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Explains which council handles cases based on the total amount of money involved in the violation.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 6. ENFORCEMENT PROCEDURES
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Outlines how violations are reported, checked by DSWD, and resolved through hearings.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 7. PROHIBITED ACTS
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Lists what is banned: beneficiaries cannot use their 4Ps cards as collateral, and others cannot accept them or convince beneficiaries to do so.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 8. PENALTY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Sets the fines, community penalties, or suspension of business permits for anyone caught violating the law.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 9. DISPOSITION OF FINES
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Directs collected fine money into a trust fund to support 4Ps programs and livelihood projects.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 10. SUPPLEMENTAL ISSUANCES
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Allows DSWD and CSWD to issue further guidelines to help enforce this law.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 11. REPEALING CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Cancels older rules that go against this new ordinance.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 12. SEPARABILITY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: Ensures that if one part of this law is found invalid, the rest remains active.

articles_and_sections.title: SECTION 13. EFFECTIVITY CLAUSE
articles_and_sections.eli5_explanation: States when this ordinance officially starts being enforced.

fines.penalty: Counseling and a written warning from the DSWD.
Counseling by DSWD and suspension of household grants for one payment period (2 months).
Delisting of the household from the 4Ps program (non-appealable).
Php2,500.00 per violation and surrender of the Pantawid Cash Card to DSWD.
Php3,500.00 per violation, surrender of cash card, and 3 months suspension of business permit or blacklisting.
Php5,000.00 per violation, surrender of cash card, and cancellation/revocation of business permit or blacklisting.
Php3,500.00 per violation, surrender of cash card, and a written warning attached to service record.
Php5,000.00 per violation, surrender of cash card, and administrative disciplinary action under Civil Service Rules.

eli5_summary: It is now illegal for anyone in Zamboanga City—including businesses, loan sharks, and government workers—to take 4Ps cash cards or IDs as security for loans. Beneficiaries are also barred from pawning their cards. Anyone caught doing this faces heavy fines, suspension of business permits, or removal from the 4Ps program.
governing_agency: Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) and City Social Welfare and Development Office (CSWD)
